commands.name: agent_thread_append_messages

args.name: input
args.type: AppendAgentThreadMessagesInput { operationId, expectedHeadMessageId: string|null, messages: NewAgentThreadMessage[] }

commands.returns: AgentThreadMessage[] — only the newly appended rows, in order, with DB-assigned contiguous seq
sideEffects: one SQLite transaction commits the message batch and its idempotent response record together
bumps the thread's updatedAt / transcript head
commands.callerUsage: appendThreadMessages() diffs current messages against the persisted baseline (persisted must be an exact prefix), sends only the tail, sets expectedHeadMessageId = last baseline id ?? null, and reuses ONE in-flight operationId per thread (pendingTranscriptAppends) so a lost IPC response can be retried for the exact committed result. It then verifies returned rows are same-thread, id/role-matched, and contiguous with the previous seq.
commands.notes: COMPARE-AND-SWAP: the Rust command COLLAPSES the typed AgentThreadAppendOutcome::HeadMoved variant into a plain Err string ("Agent transcript changed before append (expected X, found Y); reload the conversation before retrying"). SMELL: a structured, expected outcome is only distinguishable by parsing an error message over IPC — a port should consider surfacing the variant. `expectedHeadMessageId: null` explicitly asserts an empty transcript (not 'don't care'). Per-message `id` is optional (server generates a uuid) but the frontend always supplies the UIMessage id; `seq` is never caller-supplied. Never rebases implicitly — the caller must reload or fork.

commands.name: agent_thread_create

args.name: input
args.type: CreateAgentThreadInput { requestId, agentKind, subjectKind?, subjectId?, implementationId?, venueId?, scoreId?, title? }

commands.returns: AgentThread { id, ownerUserId, agentKind, subjectKind, subjectId, implementationId, venueId, scoreId, forkedFromThreadId, forkedAtMessageId, title, createdAt, updatedAt }
sideEffects: inserts the thread row (SQLite) AND initializes/attaches its authored document in the same operation
idempotent on requestId — a retried identical payload returns the previously created thread instead of a duplicate
commands.callerUsage: createThread(input) wraps it as `{ input }`; createScopedThread builds requestId=crypto.randomUUID(), never sends the principal, retries once with the SAME payload on failure (relying on requestId idempotency), then fail-closed validates the returned row with threadMatchesScope().
commands.notes: Owner is derived from auth::admitted_principal(db) — the caller CANNOT set ownerUserId; `null` owner is the signed-out principal, a real value, not 'unknown'. agentKind/subjectKind are plain strings on the wire but the backend enforces a closed routing invariant (models/agent_threads.rs authored_route): track_copilot requires subjectKind="track" + non-empty subjectId/venueId/scoreId and NO implementationId; pattern_graph requires subjectKind="pattern" + non-empty subjectId/implementationId and NO scoreId. Anything else errors.

commands.name: agent_thread_delete

rust.service: AuthoredDocuments::delete_thread_with_authored_state, with a retire callback over PythonWorkspaceService + GraphRunStore

sideEffects: ORDERED teardown: for each child authored workspace, PythonWorkspaceService::retire_thread(workspaceId) then GraphRunStore::forget(workspaceId); then retire_thread(threadId) and forget(threadId); only then is the thread row deleted
kills/drains sandboxed Python kernels and drops published graph runs
deletes the thread row and its authored workspaces
commands.callerUsage: deleteThread() awaits the invoke then clears the thread's entry from the pendingTranscriptAppends idempotency map.
commands.notes: Authored REVISION HISTORY survives deletion and remains restorable — this is not a cascade purge of authored state (consistent with the project's no-cascade-deletes rule). The retire-before-delete ordering is load-bearing: it closes admission so an in-flight host call can't write after the branch disappears. Needs four backend services wired (Db, AuthoredDocuments, PythonWorkspaceService, GraphRunStore).

commands.name: agent_thread_get
sideEffects: read-only SQLite query scoped to the admitted principal
commands.callerUsage: loadThreadMessages() maps rows to AI-SDK UIMessages, substituting `[{type:'text',text:''}]` for an empty parts array, validates every message with isAgentChatMessage and throws (fail-closed, no partial history) if any row fails; builds the append baseline with partsJson computed from the CLIENT message, not the echoed row.
commands.notes: Messages come back ordered by `seq` ascending; `seq` is i64 exported as TS number and is DB-assigned. `parts` is the AI SDK UIMessage.parts array verbatim — opaque JSON the backend never interprets; it round-trips through serde_json and MAY have object keys reordered, so never byte-compare the echoed parts. A thread owned by another principal is not visible (scoped by ownerUserId).

commands.name: agent_thread_list
sideEffects: read-only SQLite query scoped to the admitted principal
commands.callerUsage: listThreads() explicitly sends `?? null` for each filter (never omits them); listScopedThreads() then re-filters client-side on the full ExactThreadScope (principal, implementationId, venueId, scoreId) because the command has no filter for those fields.
commands.notes: Each filter is an independent AND; null = wildcard for that field. Backend orders newest-first but the frontend deliberately re-picks with newestThread() (updatedAt desc, createdAt tiebreak) so behavior doesn't depend on SQL ordering — a port should not rely on the server order. No pagination. Three of the seven identity fields are NOT filterable server-side; that filtering must happen in the client.

commands.name: agent_thread_rename
sideEffects: updates title (and updatedAt) on the thread row, scoped to the admitted principal
commands.callerUsage: renameThread(threadId, title) passes the title through unchanged; `null` is a real value meaning 'clear the title'.
commands.notes: Title is display metadata and is deliberately NOT part of ExactThreadScope / thread identity. No idempotency key — last write wins.

commands.name: authored_state_merge_workspace_into_workspace

args.name: input
args.type: MergeAuthoredWorkspaceIntoWorkspaceInput { threadId: string; workspaceId: string; targetWorkspaceId: string; expectedHeadRevisionId: string; operationId: string }

commands.returns: AuthoredWorkspaceMerge — internally tagged on `status`: { status: "merged", documentId: string, revisionId: string, appliedToCurrentProjection: boolean, document: AuthoredProjectedDocument } | { status: "conflicted", conflicts: AuthoredMergeConflict[] }. Errors are plain strings (Result<_, String>).
sideEffects: Resolves the admitted principal (database::local::auth::admitted_principal) — unauthenticated/unowned threads error
Takes the per-document write lock via lock_active_thread; both source and target workspace rows must be active
Writes a new merge revision into the authored document store (git-backed repo + SQLite projection) when the merge succeeds
Reads/validates on-disk workspace files for both source and target (restores missing required files from their committed revisions)
Idempotent by operationId: a recorded operation outcome replays through replay_workspace_merge_into_workspace instead of merging again
No Tauri events emitted
commands.notes: Payload is a single `input` object (not flattened args); serde is camelCase on the wire. Merges a recursive CHILD workspace head into its detached PARENT workspace — publishing to live state is the sibling command authored_state_merge_workspace. Preconditions enforced backend-side, all surfaced as error strings: workspaceId != targetWorkspaceId; source.head must equal expectedHeadRevisionId; both workspaces must be clean (no uncommitted on-disk drift) — child dirty => "commit it before merging", parent dirty => "checkpoint it before merging"; both heads must still descend from the shared base. The supervisor calls it inside a serialized parent-workspace queue and retries once on throw, relying on operationId idempotency to cover a lost response; a port must keep operationId stable across that retry. On status==="merged" the caller applies `document` to the parent runtime; on "conflicted" it keeps the proposal revision + conflicts and then removes the child workspace.

commands.name: authored_state_remove_workspace
sideEffects: Resolves the admitted principal; authorize_workspace_removal accepts already-retired rows (ownership-based, so a lost-response retry still succeeds)

PythonWorkspaceService::retire_thread(workspaceId): closes the execution admission gate permanently, cancels and drains any in-flight cell, shuts down the kernel, and rm -rf's the Python workspace directory on disk
AuthoredDocuments::remove_workspace: retires the workspace row in SQLite (transactional) and deletes the authored workspace directory from disk
GraphRunStore::forget(workspaceId): drops the in-memory latest graph run for that execution id
No Tauri events emitted
commands.notes: ORDERING IS LOAD-BEARING and must be preserved by any port: authorize -> retire python execution (drain in-flight cell) -> remove authored row+dir -> forget graph run. Retiring the Python side first is what stops a running host call from writing after the authored branch disappears. Note the Python execution namespace is keyed by workspaceId (the child execution id), not threadId. Idempotent-ish: safe to retry after a lost response because authorization does not require an active row; the closed admission gate is never reopened. Callers treat it as fire-and-forget cleanup (supervisor guards with a `workspaceRemoved` flag and calls it on failure paths and on conflict).

commands.name: cancel_python_cell
commands.returns: boolean — true if a cell was in flight and got interrupted, false if there was nothing to cancel
sideEffects: Resolves the admitted principal and verifies the thread row is visible to it
When targeting a child, verifies the authored workspace is active and owned by the thread
Cancels the in-flight cell's cancel token — the worker gets the interrupt ladder; the running run_python_cell call still returns a terminal result with status "interrupted"
No Tauri events emitted, nothing written
commands.notes: Same flat camelCase args and same executionId/authoredWorkspaceId pairing rule as run_python_cell (both or neither, and equal). Fire-and-forget at the call site: bound to abortSignal's `abort` event with { once: true }, invoked with `void ... .catch(() => {})`, and the listener is removed in the run's finally block — the return boolean is discarded. Crucially, cancelling does NOT abandon the run: the caller still awaits run_python_cell so the transcript records whatever the cell emitted before interruption. If the turn is already aborted before the cell starts, the frontend short-circuits and never invokes either command.

commands.name: run_python_cell

rust.service: commands::agent_execution::run_python_cell_inner_as_scoped (same file:325) over agent_execution::{PythonWorkspaceService, GraphRunStore, bindings::providers::assemble_bindings, track_host::TrackHost} + services::authored_documents::AuthoredDocuments

args.name: scope
args.type: PythonScopeInput { trackId, venueId, scoreId, patternId, implementationId: string|null; window: [number, number]|null (absolute track seconds); graphDefinition: unknown|null }

commands.returns: PythonCellResult { status: "ok" | "error" | "interrupted" | "failed"; stdout: string; stderr: string; repr: string|null; traceback: string|null; figures: PythonCellFigure[] { artifactRel, width, height, base64Png }; notices: string[]; durationMs: number }
sideEffects: Resolves StorageRoot from the AppHandle and the fixtures resource root; resolves the admitted principal
Claims a per-execution cell lease (one cell at a time per execution id) and starts/reuses a sandboxed persistent Python kernel process for that execution
Assembles a fresh binding revision into the workspace artifact store — writes binding files into the workspace dir on disk
Runs arbitrary user/model Python; through TrackHost the cell can mutate authored track state (only when the thread scope + owner authorize an edit scope AND a durable user turn message is supplied)
Reads figure PNGs back off disk, registers them as outputs in the artifact store, and base64-encodes them into the response
No Tauri events emitted; results are returned synchronously to the caller
commands.notes: Args are FLAT camelCase (not wrapped in `input`) — unlike the authored_state_* commands. executionId and authoredWorkspaceId must be supplied together AND be equal, else the command errors ("child Python execution id must match its authored workspace id" / "...requires both..."); with neither, executionId defaults to threadId. The frontend spreads them conditionally so they are omitted rather than sent as null. `scope` must be fully explicit: the tool fills every unknown field with null (see the test at python-tool.test.ts:225) — a port that omits keys instead of nulling them changes the wire shape. Scope fields are asserted against the thread's pinned subject and rejected on mismatch; the thread, not the caller, is the authorization principal. turnMessageId must name a durable `user` message already persisted in the thread before the model call; editable cells hard-fail without it. Figure budget: 8 MB total PNG per cell, over-budget figures are dropped with a human-readable notice in `notices` rather than truncated; the frontend then drops any single figure over MAX_PERSISTED_FIGURE_BYTES when storing, keeping width/height. `status: "error"` = Python exception (kernel healthy), `"failed"` = infrastructure failure (worker died/timeout), reason always in `notices`. The caller serializes cells per execution id (enqueueCell) and converts any IPC throw into a synthetic `failed` result, so the tool never rejects.

commands.name: authored_state_check_workspace
commands.returns: AuthoredWorkspaceCheck { id, headRevisionId, snapshotId, changed, document }
sideEffects: reads the raw workspace directory; RESTORES any missing required files from the head revision
for TRACK-scope documents only, if raw files differ from head files it OVERWRITES the workspace directory with the head files (repairing a stale post-commit materialization) and reports changed=false
commands.callerUsage: checkAuthoredWorkspace(input) with `{ input }`; snapshotId feeds straight into commit's `expectedSnapshotId`.
commands.notes: NOT a pure read — it repairs the workspace on disk. `snapshotId` is a hash of the exact raw files inspected and is the compare-and-swap token for commit_workspace, so check→commit must be adjacent with no intervening writes. `changed` means raw files diverge from the detached head; for track workspaces changed is effectively always false because raw divergence is repaired rather than reported (track children author only through structured Python ops). `document` is the CANDIDATE projection decoded from raw files, which may not equal any stored revision.

commands.name: authored_state_commit_workspace

args.name: input
args.type: CommitAuthoredWorkspaceInput { threadId, workspaceId, expectedHeadRevisionId, expectedSnapshotId, operationId, message }

commands.returns: AuthoredWorkspaceCommit { id, revisionId, appliedToCurrentWorkspace, changed, document }
sideEffects: creates a new revision on the workspace's DETACHED branch (not the document head) and advances the workspace head
enqueues sync closure
commands.callerUsage: commitAuthoredWorkspace(input) with `{ input }`; expectedHeadRevisionId comes from the handle/check and expectedSnapshotId from check_workspace.
commands.notes: DOUBLE compare-and-swap: both expectedHeadRevisionId AND expectedSnapshotId must still hold. `operationId` is a validated idempotency token; `message` is normalized to a subject line (normalized_subject) and is required. Note the field is `appliedToCurrentWorkspace` here, whereas turn/restore/merge results use `appliedToCurrentProjection` — the semantics differ (workspace detached head vs document head) and a port must not unify them. Commit does NOT touch the document head; merge_workspace does.

commands.name: authored_state_create_workspace

rust.service: AuthoredDocuments::create_workspace (services/authored_documents/workspaces.rs:52), result narrowed by the local workspace_handle() helper

sideEffects: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(owner_thread_id, request_id) DO NOTHING into authored_subagent_workspaces (idempotent reservation)
materializes the revision's files into a bounded plain directory on disk (the workspace path)
commands.callerUsage: createAuthoredWorkspace(input) with `{ input }`; only id/baseRevisionId/headRevisionId reach the frontend.
commands.notes: The absolute workspace PATH is deliberately never serialized across IPC — AuthoredWorkspace (internal) has `path`, AuthoredWorkspaceHandle (IPC) does not, and there is a unit test (authored_state.rs:262) asserting the path never leaks. A port must keep that boundary. `requestId` is the idempotency key, validated as a token; reusing it against a different base/document errors ('workspace request id is already bound to another base or document'), and a retired request errors too. headRevisionId == baseRevisionId at creation. Workspace file limits: max 8 files, 16 MiB per file, 64 MiB total.

commands.name: authored_state_current_revision
sideEffects: read-only, but takes the thread's active-thread lock while reading
commands.callerUsage: currentAuthoredRevision(threadId) — flat payload. Its revisionId is the only valid `expectedBaseRevisionId` for authored_state_create_workspace.
commands.notes: This is the read-then-create handshake for workspaces: read head here, pass it as expectedBaseRevisionId so allocation is pinned to an exact revision rather than 'whatever is current'. Errors if the thread is not active/admitted.

commands.name: authored_state_finalize_turn
commands.returns: AuthoredTurnCommit — tagged by `status`: { status:'committed', documentId, revisionId, appliedToCurrentProjection, changed, document } | { status:'conflicted', documentId, preparedRevisionId, conflicts: AuthoredMergeConflict[] }
sideEffects: commits the prepared revision into the document lineage (may 3-way merge against a head that advanced)
enqueues sync closure; retires/consumes the turn preparation row
commands.callerUsage: finalizeAuthoredTurn(input) with `{ input }`; callers must branch on `status`.
commands.notes: A conflict is a NORMAL return value, not an error — do not treat non-committed as failure. On 'committed', `revisionId` is this operation's revision even if the head has since advanced; `appliedToCurrentProjection` tells you whether it is still the head, while `document` is ALWAYS the current projection and safe to hydrate. `changed` distinguishes a no-op commit. Conflicts carry a structured path (AuthoredMergePathSegment discriminated on `kind`/`value`) with base/ours/theirs as {state:'missing'} | {state:'present', value:unknown}; score_layer values are TS `number`, deliberately not bigint.

commands.name: authored_state_fork_workspace
sideEffects: reserves a new workspace row idempotently on (ownerThreadId, requestId)
materializes a copy of the SOURCE workspace's detached head files into a new bounded directory
commands.callerUsage: forkAuthoredWorkspace(input) with `{ input }`. No headless-smoke coverage found for this one.
commands.notes: Forks from another workspace's detached head, not from the document head — so the child inherits uncommitted sibling work. Same path-free handle contract and same requestId idempotency as create_workspace. SMELL: only one caller and no smoke/e2e coverage in the harness, unlike its siblings.

commands.name: authored_state_list_history
sideEffects: read-only
commands.callerUsage: listAuthoredHistory(threadId, cursor = null, limit = 100) — the 100 default lives in TS, not in Rust.
commands.notes: Cursor is OPAQUE and stable over the union of current-lineage revisions and superseded proposal tips — never construct or parse it. Entry fields: revisionId, parentIds[] (merge revisions have >1), message, authoredAt (RFC 3339), threadId?, assistantMessageId?, kind (AuthoredOperationKind, snake_case: initial_import|edit|agent_turn|restore|pattern_fork|workspace_merge|sync_integration|revision — `revision` is the forward-compat catch-all for newer producers, so a port must NOT exhaustively reject unknown kinds), position (current|ancestor|superseded — superseded tips are still restorable), proposalSequence (i64 exported as `number | null`; server-assigned cross-device ordering), and conversationCheckpoint {threadId, assistantMessageId} present ONLY when the revision sits exactly on an immutable assistant-turn boundary — i.e. it gates whether state_and_conversation restore is offerable. `limit` being null means the backend default applies.

commands.name: authored_state_merge_workspace
commands.returns: AuthoredWorkspaceMerge — tagged by `status`: { status:'merged', documentId, revisionId, appliedToCurrentProjection, document } | { status:'conflicted', conflicts: AuthoredMergeConflict[] }
sideEffects: 3-way merges the workspace's detached head into the parent document and writes a merge revision (parentIds has 2 entries in history)
enqueues sync closure; on conflict nothing is written
commands.callerUsage: mergeAuthoredWorkspace(input) with `{ input }`; callers branch on `status`.
commands.notes: Conflicted is a normal outcome, not an error. Note the ASYMMETRY with AuthoredTurnCommit::Conflicted: this variant carries ONLY `conflicts` — no documentId, no preparedRevisionId — so a shared conflict-rendering component cannot assume those fields. `expectedHeadRevisionId` is the workspace head CAS (the document head may have advanced; that's what the merge resolves). The workspace is not automatically removed after a successful merge — see authored_state_remove_workspace.

commands.name: authored_state_prepare_turn
sideEffects: takes the thread's authored write lock, inserts a new revision parented on the current head
INSERTs into authored_turn_preparations (thread_id, assistant_message_id, …) — one prepared turn per assistant message
enqueues the revision closure for sync and, when signed in, enqueues a local sync row for authored_turn_preparations
commands.callerUsage: prepareAuthoredTurn(input) invokes with `{ input }` and the returned preparedRevisionId is carried into finalize.
commands.notes: IDEMPOTENT on (threadId, assistantMessageId): a repeat returns the existing preparation, but if `graph` is supplied and its file encoding differs from the recorded snapshot it errors with 'assistant message id was already prepared with another graph'. `graph` is pattern-only: supplying it on a track thread errors ('track assistant turns cannot prepare a graph'); omitting it snapshots the current head files. `document` is the tagged union AuthoredProjectedDocument: {kind:'track_score', revision} | {kind:'pattern_graph', implementationId, revision, graph} — snake_case tag values, camelCase fields. Invariant (per project memory): one prepared authored turn per assistant row.

commands.name: authored_state_recover_turns
commands.returns: AuthoredTurnCommit[] (same tagged union as finalize, one per recovered preparation)
sideEffects: finalizes any prepared-but-unfinalized turns left behind by a crash/restart; writes revisions and sync closures for each
commands.callerUsage: recoverAuthoredTurns(threadId) — flat `{ threadId }` payload (NOT wrapped in `input`, unlike its prepare/finalize siblings).
commands.notes: Crash-recovery sweep; safe to call on load. Argument-shape inconsistency with prepare/finalize is a real ergonomics smell for a port: some authored_state commands take `{ input: {...} }`, others take flat scalars. Ordering of the returned array follows preparation order; each element must be branched on `status` exactly like finalize.

commands.name: authored_state_restore
commands.returns: AuthoredRestoreResult { documentId, revisionId, appliedToCurrentProjection, document, forkedThreadId: string|null }
sideEffects: writes a NEW forward revision (restore is roll-forward, never history rewrite)
for mode='state_and_conversation', creates a forked thread sharing the immutable transcript prefix (forkedFromThreadId/forkedAtMessageId on the new AgentThread); the original thread is left intact
enqueues sync closure
commands.callerUsage: restoreAuthoredState(input) with `{ input }`; the command handler destructures the struct itself and passes the fields positionally to the service.
commands.notes: `operationId` is a caller-owned idempotency key — retry with the same value. `mode` is snake_case on the wire. `forkedThreadId` is set ONLY for state_and_conversation and is where the UI must navigate afterwards. `document` is always the current projection; `revisionId` may already be superseded — check appliedToCurrentProjection. Restore never deletes revisions, so the pre-restore state stays in history.

commands.name: authored_state_write_workspace_graph
commands.returns: Graph (models::node_graph::Graph — the canonicalized graph, not the input echoed back)
sideEffects: canonicalizes the graph, encodes it to the host-owned workspace files (graph.json / layout.json), validates workspace limits, then REPLACES the workspace directory contents
does NOT create a revision — the detached head is unchanged until commit_workspace
commands.callerUsage: applyGraph(next) runs layoutGraph(next) client-side, invokes with `{ input: { threadId, workspaceId, graph: laidOut } }`, and REBINDS its local `graph` variable to the RETURNED value — the canonicalized result is authoritative, not the sent one.
commands.notes: Pattern threads only — errors with 'graph workspace writes require a pattern agent thread' on a track scope. This is the one authored_state command whose return type is a domain model rather than an Authored* wrapper, and the only one taking a full Graph payload (potentially large). The model never sees graph.json/layout.json; their encoding stays host-owned. Callers must treat write as canonicalizing (node ordering/ids may normalize) and must not assume idempotent byte-equality with the input.

commands.name: preview_graph_image

args.name: graph
args.type: Graph (full inline node graph: nodes, edges, args)

sideEffects: read-only; VenueAccess::<Read> on the venue
commands.notes: Same as preview_pattern_image but for an UNSAVED graph — this is the graph-editor agent's 'look at my edit' tool. Same end_time > start_time guard and same Selection-forced-to-all default args, so the pattern-editor call site pre-rewrites graph.args via overrideSelectionArgs(...) to inject the editor's preview selection before sending. Requires a selected track context (venueId falls back to the current venue id, else empty string — an empty venueId will fail VenueAccess).

commands.name: preview_pattern_image
sideEffects: read-only; VenueAccess::<Read> on the venue
commands.notes: Errors with 'end_time must be greater than start_time' if the span is non-positive — validate before calling. Args are the PATTERN DEFAULTS with every Selection-typed arg forced to `{"expression":"all","spatialReference":"global"}` (preview_arg_values), so this is not what the timeline clip would render. Without beatGrid the column count falls back to the non-beat-aligned width rule. The `_at` variant takes (pool, StorageRoot, resource_root) directly — the AppHandle only ever supplied those two roots, so a port needs no Tauri handle.

commands.name: view_composite_image
sideEffects: read-only; builds a throwaway Scene (does NOT install it on the render engine and does not touch PLAN_CACHE)
commands.notes: No venueId argument — the venue is inferred by get_accessible_venue_for_track(trackId), which errors 'No score with annotations for this track.' when none is accessible, and 'No annotations for this track/venue.' when the resolved score is empty. Smoke treats /No annotations|No score/ as a skip, not a failure. Renders Scope::Composite (all annotations blended by z/blend_mode), unlike the per-clip preview commands.

commands.name: get_discovered_nodes
commands.returns: ArtNetNode[] — { ip, name (ArtPoll short name), long_name, port_address: u16, last_seen: u64 unix secs }
sideEffects: none; clones the current map values under the manager mutex
commands.notes: SNAKE_CASE over the wire (ArtNetNode is a bare serde::Serialize with no rename_all) and the TS type in settings-dialog.tsx:55 mirrors that — second place in this fragment where the wire contract diverges from the app-wide camelCase convention. Order is HashMap iteration order — NON-DETERMINISTIC; sort client-side if stability matters. port_address is packed as (net << 8) | (sub << 4). Entries are never evicted; last_seen is the only staleness signal.

commands.name: start_discovery
commands.returns: void — SYNCHRONOUS `pub fn` returning `()`, not Result; failures are only eprintln'd
sideEffects: sets ArtNetInner.discovery_running = true; rebinds the UDP socket if not already bound
spawns a std::thread that broadcasts ArtPoll (op 0x2000) to 255.255.255.255:6454 and to a guessed /24 directed broadcast, every 3s
fills ArtNetInner.discovered_nodes from ArtPollReply (0x2100) packets, keyed by source IP
joins and replaces any previous discovery thread handle; also joined on ArtNetManager::drop
noisy println logging on every packet
commands.notes: Idempotent: returns immediately if discovery_running. No result channel and no events — the UI must POLL get_discovered_nodes (settings dialog polls at 1Hz while `scanning`). A port that wants error reporting needs a new return type; today a bind failure is invisible to the frontend. Local IP is guessed by connecting a dummy UDP socket to 8.8.8.8 and assuming /24 — wrong on non-/24 or multi-homed hosts (see the StageLinQ multi-homed lesson).

commands.name: stop_discovery
sideEffects: sets discovery_running = false (the thread exits at its next loop check, up to one socket timeout later)
ArtNetManager::rebind — may close the socket if output is also disabled
does NOT clear discovered_nodes (stale nodes persist until the next scan overwrites them by IP)
commands.notes: Called from the settings dialog's effect cleanup. Cooperative stop, not a join — a caller that immediately restarts discovery relies on start_discovery joining the old handle.

commands.name: host_load_segment

args.name: endTime
args.type: number (f32, seconds; <= 0 means to end of track)

sideEffects: decodes the file into the shared audio cache (reused by analysis)
replaces the loaded segment in the global HostAudioState — clobbers whatever host_load_track/host_load_segment loaded before
takes VisibleTrackAccess Read then re-takes Operate and commits (audit/access trail)
commands.notes: Times are absolute track seconds on the way in; the host stores start_time as segment_start_abs, so every later host_seek/host_snapshot time is RELATIVE to the segment start. Errors on an empty range or empty decode. Re-checks that the authenticated principal did not change between the read and the operate access — a port must keep that check. beatGrid is passed through to LoadedSegment but the field is `#[allow(dead_code)]` — currently write-only.

commands.name: host_load_track
sideEffects: decodes the full track into the shared audio cache
replaces the loaded segment in the global HostAudioState
loads the beat grid from the DB itself (unlike host_load_segment, which takes it as an arg)
VisibleTrackAccess Read → Operate → commit
commands.notes: Convenience wrapper for the track editor: segment start is 0.0, so snapshot times equal absolute track times. Same principal-changed guard as host_load_segment. Caller (loadTrackPlayback) discards the error if the store's trackId changed mid-flight — a load race is expected and must stay tolerated.

commands.name: host_pause
commands.returns: void (infallible — Rust fn returns `()`, not Result)
sideEffects: stops advancing the playhead; stream outputs silence
commands.notes: Returns unit, so it can never reject for an audio reason (only for IPC failure). Pausing with nothing loaded is a no-op.

commands.name: host_play
sideEffects: starts the CPAL output stream / unmutes the persistent stream for the loaded segment
commands.notes: Synchronous (non-async) command returning Result. Errors if nothing is loaded. The track-editor caller always does `host_seek(playheadPosition)` immediately before `host_play` — play does not resume from the UI playhead by itself.

commands.name: host_seek

args.name: seconds
args.type: number (f32, seconds RELATIVE to segment start)

sideEffects: moves the shared fixed-point frame index consumed by the audio thread
commands.notes: `seconds` is segment-relative, NOT absolute track time — matters for pattern-editor segments loaded with a non-zero startTime. The store's `scrub` variant optimistically sets currentTime + snapshotAtMs before firing a floating (unawaited) invoke, and handleSnapshot ignores incoming snapshot times while isScrubbing, to stop pre-seek snapshots yanking the playhead backward. Any port must preserve that ordering rule.

commands.name: host_set_loop
sideEffects: flips the atomic loop flag read by the audio thread
commands.notes: Loops the whole loaded segment when no explicit loop region is set. host_set_loop_region ALSO sets this flag, so the two commands can fight: calling host_set_loop(true) with no region loops the segment, then a later clear via host_set_loop_region(null,null) silently disables looping. Two ways to control one flag — flag as a design smell.

commands.name: host_set_loop_region
sideEffects: sets the loop region
implicitly enables looping when BOTH bounds are Some, disables it otherwise
commands.notes: The implicit `set_loop(start.is_some() && end.is_some())` is the load-bearing behaviour: clearLoopRegion passes both nulls to turn looping off. A half-specified region (one null) also disables looping rather than erroring. Store updates its local loopRegion optimistically before awaiting.

commands.name: host_set_playback_rate
sideEffects: updates the fixed-point playback-rate atomic read by the audio thread (resampling ratio)
commands.notes: The backend does NOT clamp — the caller clamps to [PLAYBACK_RATE_MIN, PLAYBACK_RATE_MAX] before invoking, and sets the store optimistically. A port that drops the frontend clamp will let a 0 or negative rate reach the audio thread. Rate changes pitch (no time-stretch).

commands.name: host_snapshot
commands.returns: HostAudioSnapshot — { isLoaded: boolean; isPlaying: boolean; currentTime: number; durationSeconds: number; loopEnabled: boolean }
sideEffects: calls refresh_progress(), which pulls the atomic frame index into the mutex-guarded state before reading
commands.notes: This is a one-shot priming read only. The steady-state channel is the `host-audio://state` Tauri event, broadcast at ~15 fps (66 ms) by HostAudioState::spawn_broadcaster with the identical payload type. Both callers `listen()` first, then invoke host_snapshot once to fill the gap before the first broadcast. currentTime is segment-relative; the frontend extrapolates between snapshots using performance.now() (getExtrapolatedHostTime). A port must ship both the event and the command.

commands.name: host_unload
sideEffects: stops playback and frees the loaded segment's sample buffer
commands.notes: No TS call sites — currently dead from the frontend's perspective. Segment memory is only reclaimed by being replaced via host_load_track / host_load_segment. Either wire it into track-editor teardown or drop it; don't port it as-is without deciding.

commands.name: get_session_item

rust.service: database::local::auth (+ SyncEngine sync_lock, AuthoredDocuments identity barrier)

sideEffects: for key == SUPABASE_SESSION_KEY only: takes engine.sync_lock, reserves the single StateDb connection, runs recover_committed_signout, may bootstrap legacy state and REFRESH an expiring token (network), begins an authored identity-switch barrier, arms write admission, and bootstraps authored live projections — rolling back write admission (leaving signed writes CLOSED) on failure
for any other key: plain read
commands.notes: This is a GETTER with heavy write side effects — the whole identity-activation path hangs off it, because Supabase's storage adapter calls it on client construction. The storage adapter IGNORES its own `_key` argument and always sends SUPABASE_SESSION_KEY ("supabase_session"); the constant is duplicated in both TS and Rust (drift risk). Non-session keys ('display_name') take a trivial path. Can block on the sync lock and on a token-refresh network call — never assume it's fast.

commands.name: log_session_from_state_db
sideEffects: prints the stored Supabase session to stdout (debug logging only)
commands.notes: DEAD COMMAND — registered in src-tauri/src/lib.rs:553 but has zero callers anywhere in src/ or scripts/. Debug-only, and it logs session material to stdout; a port should drop it rather than reimplement it.

commands.name: remove_session_item
sideEffects: non-session key: plain delete

session key: sync_lock + reserved StateDb connection, recover_committed_signout, capture auth + write-admission backups, authored identity barrier, suspend write admission, consume_signout_transition_and_clear_session, re-arm write admission for the anonymous principal (None), bootstrap authored live projections for None; staged rollback on any failure
commands.notes: Session removal is the SIGN-OUT transition, not a cache delete — but note it does NOT reset host audio / render / devices / python the way set_session_item's identity-switch branch does. wipe_database is expected to have run first (use-auth-store calls wipe_database, then signOut() which drives this). Asymmetry between the two paths is worth flagging.

commands.name: set_session_item

rust.service: database::local::auth + AuthoredDocuments + PythonWorkspaceService + GraphRunStore + HostAudioState + RenderEngine + ControllerManager + MixerManager + StemCache + AnalysisTaskGroup

sideEffects: non-session key: plain upsert into StateDb
session key: validates the Supabase JWT, takes sync_lock + the reserved StateDb connection, classifies the write as CredentialRefresh vs identity switch
CredentialRefresh (same principal): only replaces the session + re-bootstraps authored projections + recovers deleting agent threads — deliberately does NOT reset audio/render/device/python state

identity switch: suspends write admission, suspends analysis + python workspace generations, clears GraphRunStore, host_audio.unload(), render_engine.reset_for_identity_switch(), controller.disconnect(), mixer.disconnect(), stem_cache.clear(), replaces the session, re-arms write admission, bootstraps authored projections — with staged rollback (rollback_auth_switch / rollback_activated_auth_switch)
commands.notes: The single most side-effectful command in this fragment. Error strings are contractual: they distinguish 'previous session restored' from 'signed writes remain closed' and a port must preserve that distinction. Agent-thread cleanup failures are logged, never surfaced (the switch is already committed). Like the getter, the TS adapter always sends the fixed session key and ignores its own key argument.

commands.name: wipe_database

rust.service: SyncEngine (sync_files_unlocked, enqueue_dirty, push::flush_pending_with_integrator) + AuthoredDocuments::prepare_sign_out + a BEGIN IMMEDIATE tx (close_signed_write_admission, assert_signed_in_catalog_durable, wipe_signed_in_projection)

sideEffects: holds engine.sync_lock for the whole boundary (blocks pull/push)
NETWORK: sync_files_unlocked + enqueue_dirty + push::flush_pending — offline or partial sync makes the command FAIL rather than delete
re-verifies the frozen principal after network work; errors if the session changed
suspends analysis + python workspace generations; clears GraphRunStore; host_audio.unload(); render_engine.reset_for_identity_switch(); controller.disconnect(); mixer.disconnect(); stem_cache.clear()
BEGIN IMMEDIATE tx: closes signed write admission for the principal, audits every uid-bearing table + pending_ops for durability, deletes the signed-in projection, commits
recover_committed_signout after commit; prints '[auth] Signed-in database projection wiped on sign-out'
commands.notes: Fail-closed sign-out boundary: the Supabase session stays installed until this succeeds, so the store MUST call wipe_database BEFORE signOut() (which triggers remove_session_item) — reversing the order would expose the previous account. Returns Ok(()) early and harmlessly if a committed sign-out was already recovered (idempotent-ish). Refuses with 'Refusing database wipe: N operation(s) are still pending remote sync'. Only deletes the signed-in projection for the current principal — never a blanket DB delete, and never a cascade (see the no-cascade-deletes rule).

commands.name: get_display_names
sideEffects: requires auth (short-circuits to {} BEFORE the auth check when uids is empty — an empty request never errors on signed-out)
network call to Supabase
commands.notes: Sparse map: uids whose profile row has a NULL display_name are simply absent from the result, so callers must treat 'missing key' as 'unknown', not 'error'. The PostgREST filter is built by naive `uids.join(",")` string interpolation — uids containing a comma or paren would corrupt the filter (fine for UUIDs, a landmine for a port that allows other id shapes). Both callers dedupe via Set and exclude the current user; track-browser additionally diffs against already-fetched names to avoid refetching, and deliberately omits displayNames from its effect deps to avoid a loop.

commands.name: rekordbox_get_playlist_tracks
sideEffects: reads Rekordbox master.db on spawn_blocking; no writes, no events
commands.callerUsage: invoke("rekordbox_get_playlist_tracks", { playlistId: playlistKey }) — the adapter's first param `_libraryPath` is unused for Rekordbox.
commands.notes: Arg name over IPC is camelCase `playlistId` (Tauri auto-converts the Rust snake_case `playlist_id`). Handler does a redundant `playlist_id.clone()` before the move closure — dead clone, harmless.

commands.name: rekordbox_list_playlists
commands.returns: RekordboxPlaylist[] — { id, name, parentId: string|null, trackCount: number }
sideEffects: reads Rekordbox master.db on spawn_blocking; no writes, no events
commands.callerUsage: mapPlaylist() maps id->key, name->title, parentId->parentKey and hardcodes `trackCount: 0` with a TODO.
commands.notes: Flat list with parentId back-references — the tree is assembled client-side. SMELL: the backend already returns trackCount but the adapter throws it away (rekordbox.ts:31 `trackCount: 0, // TODO: populate from backend`). A port should just use the field.

commands.name: rekordbox_list_tracks
sideEffects: reads Rekordbox master.db on spawn_blocking; no writes, no events
commands.callerUsage: mapped through mapTrack() into the generic DjTrack shape: key=uuid, duration=durationSeconds; fileSize/sampleRate/id are dropped by the frontend.
commands.notes: Returns the ENTIRE library unpaged (no limit/offset). RekordboxTrack: id, uuid, filePath?, filename?, title?, artist?, album?, bpm? (already /100 from the int*100 column), durationSeconds? (int seconds widened to f64), fileSize?, sampleRate? — everything except id/uuid is nullable. `uuid` is the stable source_id for Luma linking; `id` is the local content id and is NOT stable across exports.

commands.name: rekordbox_open_library
sideEffects: opens the Rekordbox master.db (auto-discovered path, SQLCipher decryption) on a spawn_blocking thread
no writes, no events
commands.callerUsage: rekordboxAdapter.openLibrary calls it with no payload, then in parallel lists playlists+tracks; only info.trackCount is surfaced and libraryPath is forced to null because Rekordbox auto-discovers its DB.
commands.notes: No arguments at all — the DB path is not caller-selectable. Every rekordbox_* read command reopens the DB fresh (with_db in subprocess.rs); there is no cached handle, so a port must expect per-call open cost. Errors are stringified (`Failed to open Rekordbox DB: ...`) or `Task join error: ...` on panic.

commands.name: rekordbox_search_tracks
sideEffects: reads Rekordbox master.db on spawn_blocking; no writes, no events
commands.callerUsage: invoke("rekordbox_search_tracks", { query }); `_libraryPath` ignored.
commands.notes: Search is server-side over the Rekordbox DB; no result cap is applied at the command layer. Same redundant `query.clone()` as above.

commands.name: engine_dj_default_library_path
commands.notes: Pure path construction: dirs::audio_dir() (or ~/Music fallback) + 'Engine Library'. Does NOT check existence — always Ok — so callers probe with engine_dj_open_library and fall back to a directory picker seeded with this path. to_string_lossy means non-UTF8 paths are silently mangled rather than erroring.

commands.name: engine_dj_get_playlist_tracks
sideEffects: opens/closes a read-only pool
commands.notes: Joins Track to PlaylistEntity on listId, ordered by title — NOT by the DJ's manual playlist order (PlaylistEntity has ordering columns that are ignored). Non-recursive: child playlists' tracks are not included. The generic adapter carries playlist keys as strings and converts with Number(playlistKey); an unknown id returns [] rather than erroring.

commands.name: engine_dj_import_tracks

rust.service: engine_dj::db + services::tracks::engine_dj_fast_import + tracks_db::get_track_by_id + services::tracks::run_background_analysis via AnalysisTaskGroup

commands.returns: TrackSummary[] — one per requested id, in request order (includes already-imported duplicates)
sideEffects: emits 'engine-dj-import-progress' (ImportProgressEvent { done, total, currentTrack, phase: 'importing', error? }) before each track and once more at completion
copies audio into Luma storage, computes track hash, extracts album art to $APPCONFIG/tracks/art
inserts track rows in the local DB
spawns a background AnalysisTaskGroup job (beats/stems/waveforms) for NEW tracks only, which emits its own progress events
commands.notes: Two phases: fast DB import (awaited) then detached analysis (not awaited) — the promise resolving does NOT mean tracks are analyzed. Progress `done` is the 0-based index BEFORE the track is imported, so it lags by one until the final event where done === total. Fail-fast: a missing audio file or unknown engine id aborts mid-loop with an Err, leaving previously imported tracks committed and no error event emitted (the store must handle a rejected promise while a progress listener is attached). Dedup is by source_id ('<databaseUuid>:<engineId>') then by content hash, so re-importing returns the existing track with is_new=false and skips analysis. Requires a current user id from auth (state DB) and an AnalysisTaskGroup lease — cancellation is via import_guard.checkpoint() between tracks.

commands.name: engine_dj_list_playlists
commands.returns: EngineDjPlaylist[] { id: number; title: string; parentId: number|null; trackCount: number }
sideEffects: opens/closes a read-only pool
commands.notes: Flat list ordered by title, NOT a tree — parentId (Playlist.parentListId) must be assembled client-side. trackCount comes from a separate GROUP BY over PlaylistEntity, defaulting to 0 for playlists with no entries. i64 ids serialize as JS numbers (ts-rs override) — fine in practice for Engine's autoincrement ids. Issued in a Promise.all with engine_dj_list_tracks, so it opens a second concurrent pool on the same file.

commands.name: engine_dj_list_tracks
commands.returns: EngineDjTrack[] { id: number; path: string; filename: string; title|artist|album: string|null; bpmAnalyzed: number|null; length: number|null; originDatabaseUuid: string|null; originTrackId: number|null }
sideEffects: opens/closes a read-only pool
commands.notes: Unbounded — returns the whole library in one shot (no limit/offset); the adapter maps every row through mapTrack. `path` is relative to the library root (typically '../../Music Library/x.mp3') and must go through engine_dj::resolve_engine_path, which joins then canonicalizes. length is CAST(length AS REAL) because Engine stores it inconsistently.

commands.name: engine_dj_open_library
commands.returns: EngineDjLibraryInfo { databaseUuid: string; libraryPath: string; trackCount: number }
sideEffects: opens and closes a read-only SQLite pool on <libraryPath>/Database2/m.db
commands.notes: libraryPath is the Engine Library ROOT folder, not the .db file — the command appends Database2/m.db. Errors (string) when the file is missing, and both callers deliberately use that error as an existence probe before showing a folder picker. Pool is read-only, max_connections=1, opened and closed per call — no long-lived lock on the user's library. databaseUuid is the prefix of Luma's source_id ('<uuid>:<engineTrackId>').

commands.name: engine_dj_search_tracks
sideEffects: opens/closes a read-only pool
commands.notes: LIKE '%query%' across title/artist/filename, ORDER BY title, LIMIT 200 — the cap is silent, the UI shows no truncation indicator. Query is bound (no injection) but '%' and '_' in user input are NOT escaped and act as wildcards. Searches the whole library, ignoring the currently selected playlist; the store restores the playlist view when the query is blanked.

commands.name: engine_dj_sync_library
commands.returns: EngineDjSyncResult { updated: number; missing: number; newCount: number }
sideEffects: updates title/artist/source_filename on already-imported tracks whose Engine metadata drifted
commands.notes: NO TS CALL SITE — registered in lib.rs:635 but unreachable from the UI; dead command or an unfinished feature. Never deletes (consistent with the no-cascade-deletes rule): `missing` is only counted and reported. `newCount` counts Engine tracks not yet in Luma; it does not import them. filename_changed defaults to TRUE when the local source_filename is NULL, so the first sync after an older import will rewrite metadata for every such track and inflate `updated`. O(n) per-track DB round trips over the whole Engine library plus a full local list_tracks — no batching.

commands.name: rekordbox_import_tracks

rust.service: crate::services::tracks::dj_fast_import + run_background_analysis; State<Db>, State<StateDb>, State<StemCache>, State<AnalysisTaskGroup>, AppHandle

commands.returns: TrackSummary[] — one row per requested uuid, in request order (includes already-existing tracks)
sideEffects: emits `rekordbox-import-progress` (ImportProgressEvent { done, total, currentTrack: string|null, phase: "importing", error: null }) once per track before its insert, plus a final done==total event
copies each source audio file into app storage and computes a content hash (dj_fast_import -> ensure_storage/compute_track_hash)
inserts track rows into the local SQLite DB with source_type="rekordbox", source_id = Rekordbox UUID, owned by the current user id
spawns background analysis (beats/stems/waveforms) for NEW tracks only, which later emits `track-import-progress` (tuple [trackId, step]) from services/tracks.rs:84
takes an AnalysisTaskGroup lease/epoch guard; checkpoints between tracks so a cancel/epoch bump aborts mid-import
commands.callerUsage: invoke("rekordbox_import_tracks", { trackUuids: trackKeys }) and the TrackSummary[] is returned straight out of the adapter; progress is observed via the adapter's `progressEvent: "rekordbox-import-progress"`.
commands.notes: Two-phase: phase 1 is synchronous DB import (the awaited return), phase 2 is fire-and-forget analysis — the promise resolves long before tracks are analyzed. Fails the WHOLE call (Err, partial DB writes retained) if any uuid is missing from the library, has no filePath, or the file doesn't exist on disk. Dedup is by (source_type, source_id): re-importing returns the existing track with is_new=false and skips analysis. PERF SMELL: it calls subprocess::list_tracks() to load the entire library then does a linear `find` per uuid — O(n·m); there is no by-uuid subprocess lookup. Requires an authenticated user (auth::get_current_user_id) unlike the read-only rekordbox commands.

commands.name: get_node_types
commands.returns: NodeTypeDef[] — { id, name, description?, category?, inputs: PortDef[], outputs: PortDef[], params: ParamDef[] }
commands.notes: Synchronous (non-async) command, no Db/State deps — pure static catalog built in Rust. Returns Result-less Vec, so it can never error. Frontend loads it lazily only on pattern routes into a store; the pattern editor appends a synthetic `patternArgsNodeDef` client-side, so the node catalog the editor uses is NOT purely this response.

commands.name: run_graph

args.name: context
args.type: GraphContext { trackId, venueId, startTime: f32, endTime: f32, beatGrid?: BeatGrid, argValues?: Record<string, unknown>, instanceSeed?: number(u64) }

commands.returns: RunResult { views: Record<string, Signal>, melSpecs: Record<string, MelSpec>, colorViews: Record<string, string>, universeState: UniverseState | null }
sideEffects: installs/clears the RenderEngine active scene (live visualizer) unless driveLivePreview === false
when agentThreadId is set: publishes the full evaluation into the agent thread's Python workspace via GraphRunStore::commit_evaluation (binds `luma.graph.run`)
venue access gates: VenueAccess::<Read> at entry, VenueAccess::<Operate> at exit + commit; errors if the authenticated principal changed mid-run
commands.notes: The command is a projection: evaluate_graph returns strictly more (time grid, primitive ids/positions, channel names, hashes) than RunResult carries. An empty `graph.nodes` clears the scene (Scene = None) rather than installing an empty plan. includeMelSpecs=false is the param-only/slider-drag path (skips FFT + heavy payload). Authorization is pinned to the durable parent thread (agentThreadId); agentExecutionId only namespaces Python workspace/run storage and defaults to thread_id. Venue fallback in the UI: `selectedInstance.venueId ?? currentVenue?.id ?? ""` — an empty venueId resolves selection to zero fixtures (black output), it is not an error. src/features/patterns/agent/graph-subagent-tools.test.ts:72 is NOT an IPC call site — it asserts an agent tool named `run_graph` exists.

commands.name: preview_pattern
commands.returns: UniverseState[] — one frame per sample time
sideEffects: VenueAccess::<Read> at entry, VenueAccess::<Operate> + commit at exit; errors if the principal changed mid-render
does NOT touch the render engine / live scene
commands.notes: Clamps: fps into [10, 30]; frame_count = ceil(duration*fps) clamped into [1, 256] — so a long span silently under-samples. Errors on duration <= 0 and on an empty pattern graph ("Pattern produced no output"). Args come from the pattern's own defaults with every Selection arg forced to "all" (merge_arg_values(graph, None, true)) — the hover card has no venue selection context, so preview colors/coverage will differ from a real run. Caller derives [startTime, endTime] from the enclosing downbeat bar and returns { frames, durationSec } with a cancel token; durationSec is recomputed frontend-side, the backend does not return it.

commands.name: create_pattern
sideEffects: creates the pattern's authored document (per-document Git repo) + SQLite projection
engine.push_notify.notify_one() — wakes the sync push loop
commands.notes: Idempotent on requestId: retrying the same request returns the same pattern. Owner uid resolved server-side from StateDb auth (get_current_user_id) — never passed by the caller, and Option, so an unauthenticated create is allowed with uid = null. Name is normalized to snake_case in the frontend (toSnakeCase) before sending, not in Rust. The dialog keeps the requestId in a ref keyed by a fingerprint of [name, description] so an edited retry gets a fresh key. Category is a separate follow-up set_pattern_category call — creation and categorization are not atomic.

commands.name: create_pattern_category
sideEffects: inserts a category row owned by the current uid
commands.notes: DEAD from the frontend: registered in src-tauri/src/lib.rs:470 but no TS call site anywhere in src/ or scripts/ — categories can only be listed and assigned, never created, from the UI. Also has no idempotency key (unlike create_pattern) and no sync push_notify. Either wire it up or delete it.

commands.name: fork_pattern

args.name: input
args.type: ForkPatternInput { sourcePatternId, sourceImplementationId, requestId } (camelCase both ways)

commands.returns: ForkPatternResult { pattern: PatternSummary, implementationId, documentId, revisionId, appliedToCurrentProjection }
sideEffects: creates a new pattern + implementation + authored-document revision in the Git-backed authored store and its sqlite projection
engine.push_notify.notify_one()
uid may be None (unauthenticated fork is allowed — passed as Option to the service)
commands.notes: requestId is a CALLER-OWNED IDEMPOTENCY KEY: replaying the same requestId returns the same target pattern/implementation/revision rather than forking twice. A port must generate it client-side and reuse it on retry, never regenerate per attempt. Payload is nested under a single `input` key (invoke('fork_pattern', { input })), unlike every other command here which spreads its args. The caller uses only result.pattern and drops implementationId/documentId/revisionId/appliedToCurrentProjection.

commands.name: get_pattern
commands.returns: PatternSummary { id, uid?, name, description?, categoryName?, createdAt, updatedAt, isVerified, authorName?, forkedFromId? }
commands.notes: Errors (not null) when the id is unknown. Used as a re-read after set_pattern_category and after verify_pattern, because neither returns the refreshed summary — a read-after-write round trip the port should expect.

commands.name: get_pattern_args
commands.notes: Loads the whole graph document and throws away everything but `args` — same work as get_pattern_graph_document plus venue scoping. Both call sites pass implementationId: null and rely on venueId to pick the implementation; perform-page caches on the composite key `${venueId}:${patternId}`, which is the correct invalidation key because the args returned genuinely depend on the venue. Errors are swallowed per-pattern in track-editor (falls back to []).

commands.name: list_pattern_categories
commands.returns: PatternCategory[] { id, uid?, name, createdAt, updatedAt }
commands.notes: Unscoped by user despite the uid column. Both call sites load into ad-hoc local component state (no shared store) and swallow errors to console — duplicated fetch logic worth hoisting into one store in a port.

commands.name: list_patterns
commands.notes: No venue or user scoping and no pagination — returns every local pattern; the store filters client-side (`mine` by uid, `verified` by isVerified). track-editor's loadPatterns fans out one get_pattern_args call per returned pattern (N+1 over IPC).

commands.name: search_patterns_remote
commands.returns: SearchPatternRow[] { id, uid, name, description, is_verified, author_name, category_name, created_at, updated_at }
sideEffects: requires auth ('Not authenticated - please sign in first')
network call to Supabase with the user's access token
commands.notes: FIELD-CASE SMELL: SearchPatternRow has no #[serde(rename_all)], so it crosses the IPC boundary snake_case, unlike PatternSummary (camelCase) which the same store renders alongside it. A port must not blindly camelCase this one. Caller never passes categoryName (dead param at every call site) and always passes limit:50/offset:0 explicitly, so the Rust defaults are never exercised; there is no pagination UI. Failure resets searchResults to [] and only console.errors. Note SearchPatternRowRaw is a byte-identical twin of SearchPatternRow with a hand-written From impl — duplication worth collapsing.

commands.name: set_pattern_category
sideEffects: writes the pattern's category column
commands.notes: Argument name is `patternId` here but `id` on every other pattern command — a drifted parameter naming convention worth unifying in a port. Does NOT notify the sync engine (unlike create/update/delete), so a category change is not pushed until some other write wakes the loop. Returns nothing, so callers must re-invoke get_pattern to refresh.

commands.name: update_pattern
sideEffects: engine.push_notify.notify_one()
commands.notes: Full replace, not a patch — both fields are always written. Renaming sends `description: pattern?.description ?? null` and editing the description sends `name: pattern?.name ?? ""`, so a stale/absent local pattern can blank the other field (rename-with-unloaded-pattern would write an empty name). Unlike create/delete this bypasses AuthoredDocuments and writes the SQLite projection directly — metadata is not part of the authored Git document.

commands.name: verify_pattern
commands.returns: PatternSummary { id, uid, name, description, categoryName, createdAt, updatedAt, isVerified, authorName, forkedFromId } (camelCase)
sideEffects: requires auth; errors 'You can only verify your own patterns' when pattern.uid != current uid
fetches the user's display_name from Supabase profiles (falls back to the raw uid when absent)
writes author_name AND verified locally, bumping updated_at → dirty
awaits a SYNCHRONOUS push (engine.run_push(&uid)) — not the usual notify_one nudge
commands.notes: Strict 5-step ordering: auth+ownership → profile fetch → local writes → blocking push → re-read and return. The blocking push makes this the slowest pattern command and it fails the whole call if the network is down, even though the local writes already landed (partial-apply hazard). Side effect worth flagging: verifying also rewrites author_name — a caller can't verify without stamping the name. The TS caller discards the returned PatternSummary entirely and re-invokes refresh().

commands.name: delete_pattern
sideEffects: archives (soft-deletes) the authored pattern document
engine.push_notify.notify_one()
commands.notes: Archive, not hard delete — consistent with the project's no-cascade-deletes rule. Principal comes from StateDb auth server-side; ownership enforcement lives inside archive_pattern, not in the command. Store calls refresh() (list_patterns) afterwards rather than removing optimistically.

commands.name: get_pattern_graph_document

args.name: implementationId
args.type: string | null (null = resolve the default/visible implementation)

commands.notes: Existence-checks the pattern first (get_pattern_pool) so an unknown id errors before document resolution. Passes venue_id = None, so implementation resolution here is venue-agnostic — get_pattern_args does the same load WITH a venue and can therefore resolve a different implementation for the same pattern. `revision` is the mandatory optimistic-concurrency base for save_pattern_graph_document. Callers must re-check `implementationId` in the response against what they asked for: both graph-agent and pattern-editor throw if the resolved implementation differs. smoke.ts:509 invokes it with `{}` deliberately to assert the missing-required-argument error path.

commands.name: save_pattern_graph_document

args.name: operationId
args.type: string (idempotency key for the authored write)

sideEffects: commits a revision to the pattern's authored Git document + refreshes the SQLite projection
engine.push_notify.notify_one() only when result.changed
commands.notes: The returned `graph` is authoritative and may differ from what was sent (normalization) — the caller replaces its local state with a structuredClone of it, re-derives patternArgs from graph.args, and stores the new revision as the next baseRevision. `changed: false` means a no-op save (identical content). Two post-conditions are enforced in Rust and surface as plain error strings: the projection must be a PatternGraph (not a track projection) and its implementation_id must equal the requested one. The caller sends the whole invoke payload object straight through (`save: (input) => invoke("save_pattern_graph_document", input)`), so the TS input object's keys ARE the command's arg names — renaming one breaks silently at runtime. A fingerprint check skips the call when the graph is unchanged, and a generation gate (graphAuthorityGateRef) rejects the result if a newer load superseded it.

commands.name: perform_match_track
commands.returns: PerformTrackMatch { trackId: string|null, hasAnnotations: bool, filename: string } (camelCase)
sideEffects: opens a read transaction on the venue; no writes
commands.notes: StageLinQ path only — the Pioneer branch of the same store function calls the sibling perform_match_track_by_metadata (title/artist/bpm/durationSecs/venueId) instead. Never errors on 'not found': returns trackId=null with filename='' when the network path can't be parsed, and trackId=null with the parsed filename when no track matches. Takes tracks.first() with no tie-break, so duplicate filenames silently resolve to an arbitrary row. Track lookup is by source filename and is NOT venue-scoped, but the scores lookup IS — a track can match while hasAnnotations is false purely because the score lives in another venue. Caller guards a race by re-checking that the deck still holds the same track_network_path before applying the result.

commands.name: perform_match_track_by_metadata
commands.returns: PerformTrackMatch { trackId: string | null, hasAnnotations: boolean, filename: string } (serde camelCase)
sideEffects: none — read-only; takes a VenueAccess<Read> lease on VenueResource::Venue(venue_id)
commands.notes: Pro DJ Link path only (StageLinQ uses perform_match_track). Match cascade is ordered: duration ±5s window (queried against the raw pool, NOT through the venue access lease) → BPM filter (exact/×2/÷2, 5% tolerance; passes through when either side has bpm<=0) → bigram Jaccard similarity of normalized 'title artist', min score 0.25, sorted desc, best wins. Empty title AND artist short-circuits to a null match. `filename` falls back to the basename of file_path (split on '/', so Windows paths would not split) when source_filename is null; on a miss it is "" not null. trackId is the only nullability signal.

commands.name: prodjlink_connect
sideEffects: claims the given device number on the Pro DJ Link network and starts the client
streams DeckEvent to the webview as `perform_event`
commands.notes: Pioneer CDJs (not Denon). deviceNum is the virtual player number this app claims — must not collide with a real deck; the UI defaults to 7 and the store falls back to 7 (`deviceNum ?? 7`). Same event-listener-before-invoke ordering requirement as stagelinq_connect; the two connects share one code path in the store selected by `source`.

commands.name: prodjlink_disconnect
sideEffects: stops the client, releases the claimed device number, `perform_event` emission ceases
no-op when nothing is running
commands.notes: Mirror of stagelinq_disconnect; the store picks between them on `source` and ignores errors from either.

commands.name: prodjlink_discover
commands.returns: DiscoveredDevice[] { player: u8, name, ip } — snake/flat, no rename_all; unique, sorted by player number
sideEffects: binds UDP port 50000 and passively listens for CDJ keepalives for a HARDCODED 3 seconds — the command blocks that long
no device-number claim, so it is safe to call while not connected
commands.notes: Returns Vec (never errors) — an empty list means 'nothing heard', not failure; if the socket can't bind, discover_cdjs also returns []. So a port cannot distinguish 'no CDJs' from 'networking broken'. The 3000ms timeout is not a parameter. TS mirrors the shape locally as `interface DiscoveredCDJ` in perform-page.tsx rather than using a generated binding — a hand-copied type that will drift.

commands.name: render_clear_active_layer
sideEffects: sets RenderEngine.active_scene = None so the render loop emits nothing for the editor layer; takes VenueAccess<Read>
commands.notes: Editor-side counterpart to render_clear_perform: only the active (track/pattern editor) scene, not deck layers. Universe designer pairs it with clearing the frontend universe + dmx stores so fixtures read as off.

commands.name: render_clear_perform
sideEffects: clears perform_layers, perform_deck_states and all cue_buffers; leaves manual_layer state intact; takes VenueAccess<Read>
commands.notes: Called on Perform page unmount, on Disconnected events and on user disconnect. Note it also wipes cue_buffers, so cues compiled by render_composite_deck_unmatched / midi_compile_cues_for_deck must be recompiled after any clear. All call sites fire-and-forget.

commands.name: render_composite_deck
sideEffects: composite_track writes the compiled Scene into RenderEngine.active_scene
promote_active_scene_to_deck moves it (take) into perform_layers[deck_id] — active_scene ends up None
reads stems via StemCache and FFT via FftService (may compute/cache analysis)
commands.notes: Two-step by design: compositing targets active_scene and is then promoted, so it transiently clobbers whatever the editor had in active_scene. Venue authorization happens inside composite_track (this fn takes no explicit VenueAccess). Callers pair it with midi_compile_cues_for_deck for the same deck+track. Reserved deck id 99 is the simulated deck (render_engine.rs SIM_DECK_ID).

commands.name: render_composite_deck_unmatched
sideEffects: installs compiled MIDI cue buffers for the deck in RenderEngine (cue_buffers), no perform_layers scene
reads fixture definitions from the resolved resources root and app storage root
takes VenueAccess<Read> on VenueResource::Venue(venue_id)
commands.notes: Used when a CDJ deck has no matching Luma track: builds a synthetic beat grid from live BPM + beat-in-bar so beat-reactive cues stay in phase. beat_number is 1-indexed (1–4 in 4/4); position_secs is playback position at load time. resolve_fixtures_root failure is swallowed to None (.ok()) — silent degradation smell. Caller only invokes when bpm > 0 and deck.song_loaded.

commands.name: render_set_deck_states
sideEffects: replaces (does not merge) RenderEngine.perform_deck_states; takes VenueAccess<Read>
commands.notes: Hot path — called on every StateChanged frame and on every mixer state change; drives crossfade blending across decks. PerformDeckInput field names are snake_case on the wire (`deck_id`), unlike every other perform payload which is camelCase — the struct has no serde rename_all. Whole-vector replace means a deck omitted from `states` immediately drops to no state. Caller filters decks with sample_rate <= 0 and computes volume = channelFader * crossfaderWeight; time = samples / sample_rate. Errors are swallowed (.catch(() => {})).

commands.name: stagelinq_connect
sideEffects: starts the StageLinQ discovery/connection client and stores it in the manager's Mutex<Option<Client>>
errors 'StageLinQ already running' if a client is live (not idempotent)
streams DeckEvent to the webview as the `perform_event` event for the client's lifetime
commands.notes: Denon/Engine DJ hardware only. The store registers its `perform_event` listener BEFORE invoking connect — required, or the first DeviceDiscovered/Connected is lost. Event payload is DeckEvent, an externally-tagged-by-`type` enum: DeviceDiscovered|Connected|StateChanged|Disconnected|Error, with StateChanged carrying DeckSnapshot { decks, crossfader, master_tempo }. DeckState/DeckSnapshot/DeckEvent fields are SNAKE_CASE on the wire (no serde rename_all) — the TS store reads deck.beat_bpm / deck.track_network_path directly.

commands.name: stagelinq_disconnect
sideEffects: takes the client out of the manager and stops it; `perform_event` emission ceases
no-op (Ok) when nothing is running — asymmetric with connect, which errors when already running
commands.notes: The store's disconnect() does more than call this: it cancels the auto-reconnect timer, unsubscribes its `perform_event` listener, fires render_clear_perform for the current venue, and swallows any error from this command. Ordering: unlisten → clear render → disconnect → reset store state.

commands.name: midi_compile_cues_for_deck
sideEffects: replaces the RenderEngine group→fixture map for the venue
compiles all venue cues into RenderEngine cue_buffers keyed by (deck_id, cue_id) — stem decode via StemCache, FFT via FftService, fixture defs from resolve_fixtures_root, audio from StorageRoot
commands.notes: Unlike midi_reload_mapping this one propagates compile errors to the caller. deckId is u8 — values > 255 are a deserialization error, not a clamp. Called immediately after render_composite_deck for the same deck/track/venue; ordering matters (composite first, then cue compile). Doc comment claims it is 'called automatically after render_composite_deck' but that chaining is done in TS, not in Rust — drifted comment.

commands.name: midi_create_binding

args.name: input
args.type: CreateBindingInput { venueId: string; trigger: MidiInput; requiredModifiers?: string[]; exclusive?: boolean; mode?: TriggerMode|null; action: MidiAction; targetOverride?: Target|null; displayOrder?: number }

sideEffects: commits the write transaction
commands.notes: mode is Option<TriggerMode>; controller-config sends mode: null for continuous setIntensity bindings (no trigger semantics), and Rust falls back to TriggerMode::default() = tapToggleHoldFlash{300}. Field-name drift a port must reproduce exactly: the enum payload keys inside MidiAction / TriggerMode are snake_case (cue_id, group_id, threshold_ms) while the surrounding struct fields are camelCase — this is because the serde rename_all is on the struct, and the enum variants only rename the tag/variant name, not their fields. exclusive is set to requiredModifiers.length > 0 by controller-config.

commands.name: midi_create_cue

args.name: input
args.type: CreateCueInput { venueId: string; name: string; patternId: string; args?: Record<string, unknown>; zIndex?: number; blendMode?: BlendMode; defaultTarget?: Target; executionMode?: CueExecutionMode; displayX?: number; displayY?: number }

commands.returns: Cue (fully materialized row incl. id, uid, createdAt, updatedAt)
sideEffects: commits the write transaction (IMMEDIATE tx)
commands.notes: Payload is nested under a single `input` key, not flattened. Optional fields are omitted (undefined) rather than null by the caller — e.g. args is only sent when non-empty. executionMode is a tagged union built client-side: { type: 'loop', bars: n } | { type: 'trackTime' }. Caller then immediately creates a fireCue binding with the returned cue id, so create-cue + create-binding are effectively one logical operation with no transactional link (partial failure leaves an orphan cue).

commands.name: midi_create_modifier

args.name: input
args.type: CreateModifierInput { venueId: string; name: string; input: MidiInput; groups: string[] | null }

sideEffects: commits the write transaction
commands.notes: Note the nesting collision: the command argument is `input` and the struct field is also `input` (the MidiInput trigger) — payload reads { input: { venueId, name, input: trigger, groups } }. Caller sends groups: null explicitly when no groups are selected (never []). No mapping reload is triggered — controller-config's onCreated handler is what leads to midi_reload_mapping.

commands.name: midi_delete_binding
sideEffects: commits the write transaction
commands.notes: require_changed() — errors on missing id. Caller does not catch, so a failed delete rejects into the React handler unhandled.

commands.name: midi_delete_cue

rust.service: database::local::midi::delete_cue via VenueAccess::<Write> on VenueResource::Cue; then RenderEngine::remove_cue_buffers

sideEffects: commits the write transaction
drops compiled cue buffers for this cue from the RenderEngine (all decks)
commands.notes: Uses require_changed(): rows_affected != 1 errors with 'Venue resource not found', so deleting a non-existent id is an error, not a no-op — a port must not treat delete as idempotent. Buffer eviction happens after commit and is not rolled back on failure. Bindings referencing the cue are not cleaned up here.

commands.name: midi_delete_modifier
sideEffects: commits the write transaction
commands.notes: require_changed() — deleting a missing id errors ('Venue resource not found'). Bindings whose requiredModifiers name this modifier are NOT updated; they will silently stop matching. Caller follows with onChange() -> reloadData() + midi_reload_mapping.

commands.name: midi_fire_cue
sideEffects: latches the cue on in RenderEngine manual layer at cue.z_index
emits Tauri event 'controller_state' with a ControllerState snapshot
eprintln! diagnostics
commands.notes: Target resolution: All -> ResolvedTarget::All; Explicit{groups} -> Groups; FromModifiers -> falls back to ResolvedTarget::All because there are no held modifiers when firing from the UI — a real port must keep that fallback or UI-fired FromModifiers cues will target nothing. z_index is i64 in the model but cast to i8 here (silent wrap for |z| > 127). Fires latch (not flash); pair with midi_release_cue. The UI derives on/off from ctrlState.activeCueIds, which comes from the emitted event, so the event is load-bearing, not just telemetry.

commands.name: midi_list_bindings
commands.returns: MidiBinding[] { id, uid: string|null, venueId, trigger: MidiInput, requiredModifiers: string[], exclusive: boolean, mode: TriggerMode, action: MidiAction, targetOverride: Target|null, displayOrder: number, createdAt, updatedAt }
commands.notes: Ordered by display_order ASC. MidiAction is a tagged union { type: 'fireCue', cue_id } | { type: 'setIntensity', group_id: string|null } | { type: 'blackout' } | { type: 'controllerActive' }. TriggerMode is { type: 'toggle' } | { type: 'flash' } | { type: 'tapToggleHoldFlash', threshold_ms: number }. The UI filters cue bindings out of the actions list with b.action.type !== 'fireCue'.

commands.name: midi_list_cues
commands.returns: Cue[] (src/bindings/midi.ts — camelCase; args is Record<string, unknown>, zIndex/displayX/displayY numbers, blendMode, defaultTarget: Target tagged union, executionMode: CueExecutionMode tagged union)
commands.notes: Read-only, no commit. Ordered by display_y ASC, display_x ASC, name ASC — the perform canvas relies on that ordering. Venue access is authorization: an unknown/unauthorized venueId errors with a string, it does not return []. Called in a Promise.all alongside midi_list_bindings / midi_list_modifiers / list_patterns / list_groups.

commands.name: midi_list_modifiers
commands.returns: ModifierDef[] { id, uid: string|null, venueId, name, input: MidiInput, groups: string[]|null, createdAt, updatedAt }
commands.notes: Ordered by name ASC. groups is nullable — null means a named modifier with no group association (distinct from an empty array). MidiInput is a tagged union: { type: 'note', channel, note } | { type: 'controlChange', channel, cc } | { type: 'controlChangeValue', channel, cc }.

commands.name: midi_release_cue

rust.service: RenderEngine::latch_cue_off + flash_cue_off (VenueAccess::<Read> taken purely as an authorization check)

sideEffects: clears both latch and flash state for the cue
emits 'controller_state'
emits 'universe-state-update' with an EMPTY UniverseState when no cues remain active and the manual layer is inactive (clears the visualizer)
commands.notes: The Read access is acquired and immediately dropped as `_access` — it exists only to verify the caller may touch this cue; the cue row is never read. Conditional dark-frame emit is required behavior: without it the visualizer holds the last frame.
