commands.name: midi_reload_mapping
sideEffects: replaces the in-memory ControllerMappingSnapshot in ControllerManager
replaces the RenderEngine group→fixture map

compiles every venue cue into RenderEngine cue_buffers for the simulated deck (reads stems via StemCache, FFT via FftService, fixture defs from the app resource dir, storage root from StorageRoot::from_app)
writes several eprintln! diagnostics to stderr
commands.notes: Must be called after ANY cue/binding/modifier CRUD and on venue load — no CRUD command reloads the mapping itself. Expensive: it recompiles all cues (stem decode + FFT). Sim-deck compile errors are swallowed (logged, Ok returned), so a green result does not mean cues compiled — the only genuine failure mode surfaced is venue auth / DB read. Group map keys are fixture_id when head_index < 0, otherwise a per-head composite key. All three TS call sites .catch(() => {}) it. Heavy stderr logging including a dump of cue_buffers keys — production smell.

commands.name: midi_update_binding

args.name: input
args.type: UpdateBindingInput { id: string; trigger?; requiredModifiers?; exclusive?; mode?; action?; targetOverride?: Target|null|undefined; displayOrder? }

sideEffects: commits the write transaction
commands.notes: Sparse patch by binding id; venue derived from the binding. targetOverride is Option<Option<Target>> (undefined = keep, null = clear). Cue editor only ever patches { id, trigger, mode }. Same snake_case-inside-union caveat as create.

commands.name: midi_update_cue

args.name: input
args.type: UpdateCueInput { id: string; name?; patternId?; args?; zIndex?; blendMode?; defaultTarget?; executionMode?; displayX?; displayY? }

sideEffects: commits the write transaction
commands.notes: Sparse patch keyed by cue id — venue is derived from the cue, not passed. Omitted fields are left untouched; there is no way to clear args/target back to NULL (Option<T>, not Option<Option<T>> like UpdateBindingInput.targetOverride / UpdateModifierInput.groups). Drag-to-move (line 276) optimistically mutates local state then fires an { id, displayX, displayY } patch and swallows errors. Does NOT recompile cue buffers — callers must follow with midi_reload_mapping to make the change audible/visible.

commands.name: midi_update_modifier

args.name: input
args.type: UpdateModifierInput { id: string; name?: string; input?: MidiInput; groups?: string[] | null | undefined }

sideEffects: commits the write transaction
commands.notes: NO TS CALL SITE — registered and reachable but currently dead from the frontend (modifiers can only be created and deleted in the UI). groups is Option<Option<Vec<String>>>: undefined = leave alone, null = clear to NULL, array = set. serde's default double-Option handling means an explicit JSON null and an omitted key are indistinguishable in some serde configs — verify before porting.

commands.name: controller_cancel_learn
sideEffects: disarms learn mode (clears the stored app_handle) so MIDI resumes normal mapping
commands.notes: Always called from an effect cleanup while `learning` is true. Same missing-venueId drift as controller_start_learn at both controller-config.tsx sites; those failures are silent (.catch(() => {})).

commands.name: controller_connect
sideEffects: opens the MIDI input connection and installs the message callback
persists venue.controller_port = port_name (VenueAccess<Write>, committed)
emits `controller_port_change` { ports: string[] } on connect
the installed callback later emits `midi_learn_captured` (learn mode) and `controller_state`, and can push `universe-state-update`
commands.notes: Ordering matters: the write lease is taken first, then connect, then the DB update, then commit — a failed connect aborts without persisting. Caller passes `currentVenue?.id ?? ""`, so an empty-string venue id reaches the backend and fails at the access layer rather than being guarded in the UI.

commands.name: controller_disconnect
sideEffects: closes the MIDI connection
clears venue.controller_port so auto-reconnect stops (VenueAccess<Write>, committed)
commands.notes: Disconnect is sticky — it deliberately forgets the preferred port, so reconnecting requires an explicit controller_connect. Same `?? ""` venue-id fallback as controller_connect.

commands.name: controller_get_state
commands.returns: ControllerState { active: boolean, masterIntensity: number, activeCueIds: string[], flashCueIds: string[], heldModifiers: string[], groupIntensities: Record<string, number> } (camelCase)
sideEffects: none — snapshot read
commands.notes: Snapshot-then-subscribe: the UI calls this once on mount to seed state, then keeps it live via the `controller_state` Tauri event which carries the identical payload. A port must emit that event on every manual-layer mutation or the UI goes stale. groupIntensities only includes groups with a non-default intensity — absent key means default, not zero. activeCueIds = latched, flashCueIds = held.

commands.name: controller_get_status
commands.returns: ControllerStatus { connected: boolean, portName: string | null, availablePorts: string[] } (camelCase via ts-rs/serde)
sideEffects: VenueAccess<Read> lease only; auto-reconnect/dead-connection detection lives in ControllerManager::status
commands.notes: Polled on a 2s interval from both the Perform page and the controller config dialog — a port must keep it cheap and idempotent. Unlike mixer_get_status the doc comment does not promise auto-reconnect, but the polling cadence implies the same contract; verify against ControllerManager::status before porting.

commands.name: controller_init_for_venue
sideEffects: seeds ControllerManager's preferred port from venue.controller_port (Option<String>) so the status poll can auto-reconnect without user action
commands.notes: Must run before the status poll starts for auto-reconnect to work. Called once per venue load alongside mixer_init_for_venue and midi_reload_mapping; errors swallowed. Takes VenueAccess<Read> but binds it `mut` even though nothing writes.

commands.name: controller_list_ports
sideEffects: none
commands.notes: Synchronous (not async), no venue argument, no authorization. Currently has no TS call site — the controller config dialog reads ports out of ControllerStatus.availablePorts instead. Dead-command candidate; a port would only need it if it does not surface ports via status.

commands.name: controller_set_active
sideEffects: enables/disables the manual (controller) render layer inside RenderEngine
commands.notes: Goes through RenderEngine, not ControllerManager, despite the `controller_` prefix — the manual layer is render state. Caller toggles against ctrlState?.active (undefined → treated as false → sends true) and guards on a truthy currentVenueId.

commands.name: controller_start_learn
sideEffects: arms learn mode: the next parseable MIDI event emits a `midi_learn_captured` event (MidiInput payload) and is swallowed instead of being mapped; learn auto-disarms after one capture
commands.notes: One-shot arm — the capture disarms itself, so a UI needs to re-arm per binding. DRIFT: both controller-config.tsx call sites invoke it with NO argument object, but venue_id is a required String — those two learn flows reject at the IPC layer and surface as setError(String(e)). Only perform-page.tsx:1026 passes { venueId }.

commands.name: mixer_cancel_learn
sideEffects: disarms learn mode so CC traffic resumes mapping to faders
commands.notes: Called from the learn-listener effect cleanup and from the dialog Cancel button; both fire-and-forget. Note it disarms learn but does NOT close a port opened by mixer_open_port — the temporary connection stays live until mixer_connect or mixer_disconnect.

commands.name: mixer_connect

args.name: mapping
args.type: MixerMapping { channelFaders: Record<u8, {channel, cc}>, crossfader: {channel, cc} | null }

sideEffects: opens the MIDI input and installs the fader callback
persists venue.mixer_port + venue.mixer_mapping_json (mapping re-serialised to JSON by the command, VenueAccess<Write>, committed)
the callback emits `mixer_state` { channelFaders, crossfader } on every fader move, and `mixer_learned` { channel, cc } while learn is armed
commands.notes: Mapping is serialised to JSON BEFORE the write lease is taken, so a bad mapping fails before touching the DB; connect precedes the DB write, commit last. channelFaders keys are 1-based deck ids (the UI builds 1..4 from fader_1..fader_4 and omits unmapped ones). After a successful connect the UI fabricates an initial MixerState with every mapped fader at 1.0 and crossfader 0.5 — the backend does not emit an initial state.

commands.name: mixer_disconnect
sideEffects: closes the MIDI connection
clears both venue.mixer_port and venue.mixer_mapping_json so auto-reconnect stops (VenueAccess<Write>, committed)
commands.notes: Destructive: the saved MAPPING is dropped too, not just the port — the user must re-learn after disconnecting. Caller then locally sets mixerState null and patches mixerStatus { connected: false, portName: null } rather than re-polling.

commands.name: mixer_get_status
commands.returns: MixerStatus { connected: boolean, portName: string | null, availablePorts: string[] } (camelCase; serialize-only, no Deserialize)
sideEffects: MixerManager::status performs dead-connection detection and auto-reconnect using the preferred config seeded by mixer_init_for_venue — this getter is NOT side-effect free
commands.notes: Documented contract: call every ~2s; the poll IS the reconnect driver. A port must not treat it as a pure read or debounce it away. Caller declares the return shape inline as an anonymous type instead of importing MixerStatus from src/bindings/mixer.ts — drifted duplicate of a generated type.

commands.name: mixer_init_for_venue
sideEffects: parses venue.mixer_mapping_json and seeds MixerManager's preferred (port, mapping) so mixer_get_status can auto-reconnect
commands.notes: Must run before the 2s status poll or auto-reconnect never fires. Corrupt/unparseable mixer_mapping_json is swallowed to None via `.ok()` — the mixer then silently reconnects with no mapping instead of erroring; empty-string json is treated as absent. Called once per venue load next to controller_init_for_venue.

commands.name: mixer_list_ports
sideEffects: none
commands.notes: Synchronous, no venue argument, no authorization — the only mixer command without a venue lease. Polled every 1.5s while the mixer dialog is open so hot-plug is detected; the dialog auto-selects ports[0] when nothing is chosen yet.

commands.name: mixer_open_port
sideEffects: opens the MIDI port with an EMPTY mapping and does NOT persist anything to the venue DB
commands.notes: Learn-flow only: lets CC traffic reach the manager before the user saves a mapping. It replaces any live connection's mapping with the default (empty channelFaders, crossfader: None), so opening a port for learn silently disarms a working mixer mapping until mixer_connect is called again — flag this when porting. VenueAccess<Read> despite mutating manager state.

commands.name: mixer_start_learn
sideEffects: arms learn: the next CC message emits `mixer_learned` { channel: u8, cc: u8 } (raw serde_json, not a ts-rs type) and is swallowed instead of being mapped to a fader; auto-disarms after one capture
commands.notes: Requires an open port — the UI calls mixer_open_port first when nothing is connected. One-shot, so the dialog re-arms per learn target. On capture the UI clears any other target already bound to the same channel+CC, enforcing uniqueness client-side only; the backend does not.

commands.name: score_dsl_export
sideEffects: VenueAccess::<Read> on VenueResource::Score(scoreId)
commands.notes: includeClipIds selects the export kind: true => ScoreDslExportKind::Canonical (round-trippable, clip ids embedded), false => Exemplar (clean source for showing an LLM). trackId+venueId are not lookup keys — they are asserted against the loaded score by require_score_scope, and a mismatch returns the deliberately opaque "Venue resource not found" (enumeration guard, not a real 404). Owner uid is read off the score row, never passed in. `revision` is the base for a later import.

commands.name: score_dsl_validate
commands.returns: ScoreDslValidationResponse { valid, baseRevision, clipCount: number | null, diagnostics: ScoreDslDiagnostic[] }
sideEffects: VenueAccess::<Read> only — nothing is written; the candidate is checked, not applied
commands.notes: Invalid source is NOT an error — it resolves with valid:false plus diagnostics; only Conflict/Storage TrackEditErrors (and the >6MiB size check) reject. clipCount is null whenever valid is false. Diagnostics are 1-indexed for line/column/endColumn (Rust spans are 0-indexed columns; +1 applied in diagnostic_with_span) and carry both structured fields and a pre-rendered `formatted` caret block for LLM consumption. Warnings only appear on the valid path, sorted by (line, column, severity) with errors before warnings; the invalid paths return a single unsorted diagnostic. `baseRevision` is the value to feed straight into score_dsl_import.

commands.name: score_dsl_import
commands.returns: ScoreDslImportResponse { documentId, revisionId, changed, document: AuthoredProjectedDocument }
sideEffects: commits a revision to the score's authored document, replacing the track's clips
VenueAccess::<Write> for the scope check, then dropped before the authored apply
commands.notes: `document` is the AuthoredProjectedDocument enum — for a score import it is the TrackScore variant ({ revision }), NOT PatternGraph; a port must handle the tagged union. The TS wrapper generates operationId with crypto.randomUUID() and retries the identical request exactly once on any failure — safe only because operationId makes the write idempotent; keep that property or the retry double-applies. Write access is taken and released before the apply, so the scope check is TOCTOU-ish relative to the authored write. Stale baseRevision surfaces as a conflict error string.

commands.name: create_score
commands.returns: Score — { id; uid: string|null; trackId; venueId; name: string|null; createdAt; updatedAt }
sideEffects: inserts a `scores` row
creates the score's git-backed authored document with an initial revision containing an empty score DSL file (SCORE_PATH)
score id is deterministic from (principal, "score", requestId) — a replayed requestId returns the existing score after fingerprint verification instead of creating a second one
commands.notes: requestId is REQUIRED and must be reused verbatim on retry — that is the whole idempotency mechanism. score-picker-dialog goes further and gates on a fingerprint of [userId, trackId, venueId, name] so a double-click reuses one requestId. Fails with 'track does not exist' if the track isn't in auth_visible_tracks. The bulk import path (track-browser:337) swallows all errors with `.catch(() => {})`.

commands.name: create_track_score

args.name: payload
args.type: CreateTrackScoreInput { requestId: string; scoreId; trackId; patternId; startTime: number; endTime: number; zIndex: number; blendMode?: BlendMode | null; args?: Record<string, unknown> }

commands.returns: TrackEditResult — { revision: string; clips: TrackClip[]; idMap: Record<string,string>; createdClipId: string | null; added: number; updated: number; removed: number; appliedToCurrentProjection: boolean }
sideEffects: commits a new revision to the score's git-backed authored document (commit message 'Create track clip')
rewrites the track_scores SQLite projection for that score
takes VenueAccess::<Write> on the score
commands.notes: Single `payload` object arg (NOT flat args like create_score — the two creation commands disagree on calling convention). requestId is the idempotency key. The created clip's stable id is `createdClipId`; find it inside `clips` (smoke.ts does exactly that) — `clips` is the FULL post-edit clip list, not a delta. `appliedToCurrentProjection: false` means a replayed operation committed historically but a newer edit is now live. No frontend caller yet — the UI creates clips through replace_track_scores; only the headless smoke test exercises this path.

commands.name: delete_score
sideEffects: archives the score's authored document (git head recorded as archived — history is preserved, not rewritten)
under VenueAccess maintenance mode, DELETEs the score's track_scores rows then the scores row from the local projection
notifies the sync engine push loop (engine.push_notify.notify_one())
commands.notes: Ownership-gated: if the score's owner != current principal it errors with the deliberately opaque 'score does not exist'. Replay-safe — an already-archived score returns Ok via completed_score_archive_replay. Arg is `id`, not `scoreId` (inconsistent with every other score command). Caller must also reset the track-editor store if the deleted score is the open one; the backend emits no event for that.

commands.name: delete_track_score

args.name: payload
args.type: DeleteTrackScoreInput { operationId: string; scoreId: string; trackId: string; id: string }

sideEffects: commits a delete revision to the score's authored document
rewrites the track_scores projection
VenueAccess::<Write> on the score
commands.notes: Deletes ONE clip. scoreId/trackId are explicit precisely so a retry after a lost success response can still resolve (the clip is already gone). track-score-commands.ts retries once with the same operationId; the second call must return Ok with removed=0 or the same result, never a missing-clip error. `clips` in the response is the full remaining clip list — callers can rebuild timeline state from it without a follow-up list_track_scores.

commands.name: list_scores_for_track
commands.returns: ScoreSummary[] — { id; uid: string|null; venueId: string|null; name: string|null; annotationCount: number; createdAt; updatedAt }
commands.notes: venueId is overloaded: empty string switches to the cross-venue `list_accessible_scores_for_track` path (pattern-editor relies on this deliberately, with a comment). `uid` is the owner user id — track-session-store uses `s.uid === userId` for ownership/read-only. `annotationCount` is a joined COUNT, used by generate-dsl-dialog to pick a non-empty exemplar score. Smell: the venue path calls VenueAccess::read TWICE, discarding the first result (scores.rs:27-28) — same pattern in list_track_scores.

commands.name: list_track_scores
commands.returns: TrackScore[] — { id; uid: string|null; scoreId; patternId; startTime: number; endTime: number; zIndex: number; blendMode: BlendMode; args: Record<string, unknown>; createdAt; updatedAt }
commands.notes: Reads the SQLite projection of the authored document, not the git document. `args` comes back as a decoded JSON object (the row stores args_json TEXT); `blendMode` is decoded from a bare string column into the BlendMode enum. Frontend passes rows through toTimelineAnnotations(rows, patterns) before rendering. Same double VenueAccess::read smell as list_scores_for_track (scores.rs:52-53).

commands.name: update_track_score

args.name: payload
args.type: UpdateTrackScoreInput { operationId: string; scoreId; trackId; id; startTime?: number|null; endTime?: number|null; zIndex?: number|null; blendMode?: BlendMode|null; args?: Record<string, unknown> }

sideEffects: commits a revision to the score's authored document
rewrites the track_scores projection
VenueAccess::<Write> on the score; rejects when payload.trackId disagrees with the score's scope
commands.notes: Idempotency key is `operationId` here, but `requestId` on create — drifted naming for the same concept. scoreId+trackId are carried explicitly so an exact retry stays resolvable even after the clip row is gone. track-score-commands.ts wraps it in retryOnce() with the SAME operationId, which is the point of the design. Every optional field is Option<T>: omitted/absent means 'leave unchanged'; there is no way to null out `args`.

commands.name: get_settings
commands.returns: AppSettings — { audio_output_enabled: bool, artnet_enabled: bool, artnet_interface: string, artnet_broadcast: bool, artnet_unicast_ip: string, artnet_net: u8, artnet_subnet: u8, max_dimmer: u8 }
sideEffects: read-only
commands.notes: SNAKE_CASE over the wire — AppSettings has no serde(rename_all), unlike every other model in the app; the TS side reads settings.max_dimmer. Storage is a string k/v table; the command applies the typing and defaults: audio_output_enabled true, artnet_enabled false, artnet_interface "0.0.0.0", artnet_broadcast true, artnet_unicast_ip "", net/subnet 0, max_dimmer 100 clamped to ≤100. Unparseable values silently fall back to the default.

commands.name: set_setting
sideEffects: upserts one settings row; update_setting also applies the live effect for artnet/audio keys (rebind etc.)
commands.notes: Everything is a STRING: booleans are "true"/"false", numbers are String(n) (`updateSetting("max_dimmer", String(clamped))`). Key names are untyped/open — the valid set exists only implicitly in get_all_settings's parser, so a typo writes a row nothing ever reads (smell: no shared key enum between get and set). The dialog always re-invokes get_settings after a write rather than trusting local state; max_dimmer writes are debounced client-side.

commands.name: delete_stage_piece
sideEffects: VenueAccess::<Write> on the piece; delete + commit
FK `parent_piece_id ON DELETE CASCADE` removes the entire descendant subtree in one call
commands.notes: The cascade is the contract a port must preserve: TS computes descendantIdsOf(id) locally and filters the whole subtree out of state after one invoke. Bulk delete (:345) only invokes for the selected roots but filters the full closure locally. Note the write scope is the deleted piece, not its descendants — descendants are removed by the FK, bypassing per-resource authorization.

commands.name: list_stage_pieces
commands.returns: Vec<StagePiece> { id, uid: string|null, venueId, meshPath, kind, label: string|null, posX..posZ, rotX..rotZ, scale, parentPieceId: string|null }
sideEffects: VenueAccess::<Read> only
commands.notes: Flat list, not a tree — parent/child is reconstructed in TS via parentPieceId (descendantIdsOf). Pose fields are parent-local when parentPieceId is set, world otherwise. Store prunes selection/hover to surviving ids on every refresh; failures are logged and swallowed (stale list stays).

commands.name: move_stage_piece
sideEffects: VenueAccess::<Write> on VenueResource::StagePiece(id); one atomic pose+reparent update, then commit
commands.notes: Move and reparent are deliberately one command so a drag onto a new parent is atomic; parentPieceId=null detaches to world space. No venue_id arg (unlike the fixture commands) — scope comes from the piece. No require_changed guard here, so moving a nonexistent id silently succeeds (asymmetric with the fixture commands). Caller mirrors the same local pose into state after the await, no optimistic update.

commands.name: place_stage_piece
sideEffects: VenueAccess::<Write> on the venue; inserts and commits. No ArtNet/event side effects.
commands.notes: `kind` is an open String server-side but a closed taxonomy in practice (floor, truss, speaker, cdj, mixer, guardrail, stand, cable_cover) and is derived in TS from the mesh registry (getStageMesh(meshPath).kind) — the vocabulary lives only on the frontend, which is a drift risk. meshPath is relative to resources/meshes/. The ghost is stored in world space and converted to parent-local by dataPoseFromWorld before the call. Caller appends the returned piece to local state and keeps the armed mesh so repeat placement works.

commands.name: rename_stage_piece
sideEffects: VenueAccess::<Write> on the piece; update + commit
commands.notes: Same non-nullable-label limitation as rename_patched_fixture — no way to clear back to null. No rows-affected check. Caller patches local state after the await (throws propagate to the UI).

commands.name: force_quit
commands.returns: void (sync fn, no Result — cannot fail)
sideEffects: terminates the process immediately with code 0
commands.notes: Lives in sync.rs only because it's the escape hatch for the upload-in-progress close guard; it is not a sync command. App.tsx listens for the backend `close-requested` event, checks useUploadProgressStore for in-flight uploads, and either shows a confirm dialog (whose 'Quit anyway' calls force_quit at :533) or calls force_quit straight away (:457). In-flight uploads are abandoned, not flushed — they resume on next launch.

commands.name: get_pending_errors
commands.returns: PendingOpError[] { id, opType, tableName, recordId, attempts, lastError: string|null } (camelCase, ts-rs → src/bindings/sync.ts)
commands.notes: NO TS caller (lib.rs:569). Hand-maps every field from pending::PendingOp into a near-identical struct — a duplicated shape whose only difference is the ts-rs/serde derive; worth collapsing. lastError is nullable.

commands.name: get_sync_status
commands.returns: SyncStatus { pendingCount: number } (i64, camelCase via serde + ts-rs export to src/bindings/sync.ts)
commands.notes: NO TS caller (lib.rs:568) despite having an exported ts-rs binding in src/bindings/sync.ts — the binding is generated and unused. Read-only count over the pending_ops table.

commands.name: retry_pending_op
sideEffects: resets attempts/last_error on the pending op row
engine.push_notify.notify_one() — wakes the background push loop immediately
commands.notes: NO TS caller (lib.rs:570). The notify_one() nudge is the canonical 'a write happened, push now' pattern used across pattern commands too; a port must keep it or pushes stall until the next loop tick.

commands.name: sync_files_v2
sideEffects: uploads/downloads track audio, album art and other blobs under the app config dir
commands.notes: NO TS caller (lib.rs:567). The `_v2` suffix is vestigial — there is no v1 command anymore, so the name is drift. Return value discarded like sync_pull.

commands.name: sync_full
commands.returns: SyncReport { pull: PullStats, pushed: number, files: FileSyncStats, errors: string[] } (serde camelCase)
sideEffects: discovery → pull → push → file sync; writes to the local sqlite DB and downloads/uploads files
emits `library-changed` to the webview after pull (orchestrator.rs:138, :185) — well before file sync completes
serialized against the background sync loop by SyncEngine.sync_lock
commands.notes: Fire-and-forget at both call sites; the SyncReport is only console.logged, never rendered — errors[] is silently discarded. App.tsx guards re-entry with module-level `syncInFlight` / `syncingForUserId` flags rather than backend state. A port must keep the `library-changed` event: the frontend refreshes patterns + venues stores off it (App.tsx listener).

commands.name: sync_pull
sideEffects: pulls remote rows into local sqlite
emits `library-changed`
commands.notes: NO TS caller — registered in lib.rs:566 only. Dead IPC surface; the pull-only path is unreachable from the UI, which always goes through sync_full. Also drops the PullStats the engine returns.

commands.name: append_render_telemetry
sideEffects: mkdir -p app_config_dir
rotates $APPCONFIG/render-telemetry.log → render-telemetry.log.1 when it exceeds 5 MiB (removing any prior .1)
appends one JSON line: { ts: RFC3339 UTC, entry: <payload> }
commands.notes: Schema-free by design — the frontend builds { event, route, data } where data carries a jsHeap snapshot (performance.memory, null on non-Chromium). Because it's a blocking sync command it runs on the IPC thread and does real disk IO per call; callers are expected to be low-frequency. Errors are swallowed by the TS side (console.error only). Only one rotation generation is kept.

commands.name: replace_track_scores
commands.returns: TrackEditResult { revision: string, clips: TrackClip[], idMap: Record<string,string|undefined>, createdClipId: string|null, added: number, updated: number, removed: number, appliedToCurrentProjection: boolean }
sideEffects: VenueAccess::<Write> on VenueResource::Score(score_id); rejects if score.uid != current principal, and if score.track_id != track_id
Commits a new revision to the score's per-document Git repo (authored state) under subject 'Replace track score'
Updates the SQLite projection of track_scores for that score
Idempotent on operation_id + request fingerprint (replay-safe); does NOT notify the sync engine (delete_score does — see issues)
commands.notes: The ONE frontend primitive for multi-clip gestures — a whole-document compare-and-swap (base snapshot vs candidate snapshot), never per-row mutations. Caller builds operationId with crypto.randomUUID() and retries the *identical* request exactly once on failure (response-loss safety depends on operationId being reused verbatim). Response may return a main tip newer than the submitted candidate, so callers must rehydrate from result.clips and remap draft ids through result.idMap (rebaseTrackScoreIds/hydrateTrackReplacement in the same file). base/candidate arrays are normalized by trackScoreSnapshot before send. TrackScore.args is free-form JSON; ids in the candidate may be client-side drafts.

commands.name: delete_track
sideEffects: recovers any previously interrupted deletions first (recover_track_deletions)
BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction: prepares the deletion plan, stages the track's files (audio, art, artifacts) for deletion on disk, deletes the row, commits — with filesystem rollback on any DB failure
the sync_delete_tracks SQLite trigger enqueues the committed row deletion for push
commands.notes: One track per call — bulk delete in the UI is Promise.all over N invocations, so a mid-batch failure leaves a partial delete (and the single catch logs only the first rejection). Errors with "Track {id} not found" on an unknown id or when the owner check rejects. Principal comes from StateDb server-side. The frontend deletes optimistically from the store BEFORE invoking and never rolls back on failure — a failed delete leaves the UI lying until the following refresh()/refreshBrowser() pair repairs it. This is a real hard delete of the track row + files (unlike delete_pattern, which archives) — the no-cascade-deletes rule is about sync, not this.

commands.name: get_classifier_thresholds
commands.returns: Record<string, number> — tag name → F1-optimal threshold
commands.notes: Synchronous (non-async) command, no DB state — reads thresholds bundled with the classifier weights. Zero args; the smoke harness still passes `{}`. Frontend uses these in place of a flat 0.5 cutoff (e.g. `vocal_chop` ≈ 0.165). Failure path in the hook degrades to `{}`, which silently reverts callers to whatever default they apply.

commands.name: get_track_audio_base64
commands.returns: { data: string; mimeType: string } — TrackAudioBase64, camelCase
sideEffects: reads the whole audio file off disk into memory
commands.notes: Whole-file STANDARD base64 — a 10 MB mp3 crosses IPC as ~13 MB of string. Only justified because the bytes are fed to an LLM FilePart. mimeType is inferred from the file extension only (mp3→audio/mpeg, wav, flac, m4a|aac→audio/mp4, ogg; anything else → application/octet-stream), never sniffed. Contrast with album art, which deliberately does NOT inline base64 (CLAUDE.md). A port must not reuse this for playback.

commands.name: get_track_bar_classifications
commands.returns: { classifications: unknown; tagOrder: unknown } | null — both fields are opaque serde_json::Value re-parsed from TEXT columns
commands.notes: Untyped payload: the backend stores two JSON blobs and only validates that they parse. camelCase rename means the wire key is `tagOrder`. Returns null when classification hasn't run; the hook maps null → null state. A port must keep the JSON passthrough — there is no Rust-side schema for the classification shape.

commands.name: get_track_beats
commands.returns: BeatGrid | null — { beats: number[]; downbeats: number[]; bpm: number; downbeatOffset: number; beatsPerBar: number } (camelCase, seconds)
commands.notes: Nullable: `null` when beat detection has not run for the track. Every caller treats null as a soft miss (catch → null, or `if (!beats) return null`). Times are absolute seconds from track start. Rust type is models::node_graph::BeatGrid, exported to src/bindings/schema.ts by ts-rs.

commands.name: get_track_drum_onsets
commands.returns: Record<string, number[]> | null — keys are the n2n class names `kick`, `snare`, `hat`, `cymbal`; values are onset timestamps in seconds
commands.notes: Null when drum transcription hasn't run. Keys are not guaranteed present individually — the e2e caller guards with `onsets?.kick`. This is the only command in this group that goes straight to the db module instead of services::tracks (minor layering inconsistency).

commands.name: import_track
sideEffects: copies the audio into app storage, writes track + metadata rows, extracts album art to $APPCONFIG/tracks/art/
leases an analysis epoch and runs/spawns the analysis pipeline (beats, stems, roots, waveforms)
emits `track-import-progress` (tuple payload `(track_id, step)`) during analysis
commands.notes: DEAD from the frontend: registered at src-tauri/src/lib.rs:474, no TS caller — the UI only ever uses the batched import_tracks. The two are not thin wrappers of each other (import_track goes through import_track_with_source with TrackSourceInfo{source_type:"file"}, import_tracks uses file_fast_import + deferred background analysis), so their progress events and phase semantics differ. Note the event payload shape mismatch: this path emits a positional tuple on `track-import-progress`, while import_tracks emits a structured ImportProgressEvent on `file-import-progress` — two event names, two shapes, one concept.

commands.name: import_tracks
commands.returns: TrackSummary[] — only the rows that imported successfully, in input order
sideEffects: phase 1: copies files into storage + DB inserts, per-file
emits `file-import-progress` with ImportProgressEvent { done, total, currentTrack, phase: "importing", error } before each file, on each per-file failure, and once at completion (done === total)
phase 2: spawns background analysis for NEW track ids only (AnalysisTaskGroup lease/epoch), which emits its own progress events
commands.notes: Per-file failures do NOT reject the command — they emit a progress event with `error` set and are omitted from the returned array, so `imported.length < filePaths.length` is the only signal of partial failure. Re-importing an existing file succeeds (is_new=false) and returns the track but skips analysis. `done` is 0-indexed during the loop and equals `total` in the final event; the UI renders `done + 1`. Resolves as soon as phase 1 finishes — analysis is still running. Caller then optionally creates one empty score per imported track to bind them to the current venue (a separate non-atomic create_score fan-out).

commands.name: list_tracks
commands.returns: TrackSummary[] (id, uid?, trackHash, title?, artist?, album?, trackNumber?, discNumber?, durationSeconds?, filePath, storagePath?, albumArtPath?, albumArtMime?, albumArtStoragePath?, sourceType?, sourceId?, sourceFilename?, createdAt, updatedAt)
commands.notes: No venue scoping, no pagination, no album-art bytes — albumArtPath is a path on disk that the frontend must run through convertFileSrc (never base64-inline it, see CLAUDE.md). Almost every field except id/trackHash/filePath/timestamps is nullable. Both the pattern-editor and generate-dsl-dialog use it as the seed of an N+1 fan-out (per-track list_scores_for_track / annotation loads) — a real candidate for a purpose-built enriched query.

commands.name: list_tracks_enriched
commands.returns: TrackBrowserRow[] { id, uid?, title?, artist?, album?, durationSeconds?, albumArtPath?, albumArtMime?, sourceType?, filePath, createdAt, bpm?, annotationCount, venueAnnotationCount, venueAnnotationCoverageSeconds, hasStorage, hasBeats, hasStems, hasRoots, hasDrumOnsets, hasBarClassifications, hasGenres }
sideEffects: with venueId: takes VenueAccess::<Read> on that venue (an auth gate the venueId=null path skips entirely)
commands.notes: The `has*` booleans are version-aware EXISTS checks against current preprocessor versions (registry::current_artifact_versions); a missing registered preprocessor falls back to version 0, which matches ANY row — so `hasX` can read true for a stale artifact when the registry lacks that table. venueAnnotationCoverageSeconds is #[sqlx(skip)], computed in Rust with overlapping intervals merged, not selected from SQL. With venueId=null the venue* counts are zero. Album art is a path, not bytes (deliberate — see CLAUDE.md). Headless scripts pass `{}` (venueId undefined => None).

commands.name: reprocess_track
sideEffects: spawns a background analysis task on the current AnalysisTaskGroup epoch (returns immediately, fire-and-forget)
re-runs the full preprocessing pipeline (beats, stems, waveforms, classifications) and writes artifacts + DB rows
emits `track-import-progress` events with payload (trackId, step) while running
mutates the StemCache
commands.notes: Returns Ok as soon as the task is spawned; there is NO completion signal in the return value — progress must be observed via the `track-import-progress` event. Both callers fire-and-forget with a .catch(console.error). Bulk reprocess loops one invoke per selected id (no batch arg), even though run_background_analysis takes a Vec<String>.

commands.name: update_track_metadata
sideEffects: updates the tracks row in the local DB
emits `library-changed` (payload: unit) on the app handle after a successful write
commands.notes: All three metadata fields are Option and are sent on every call — the caller passes `title.trim() || null`, so an empty input clears the field rather than leaving it unchanged. There is no partial-update semantic. Does NOT write tags back to the audio file, only the DB. Emit failure is propagated as an error even though the write already committed.

commands.name: get_melspec

rust.service: services::tracks::get_melspec (FftService + load_or_decode_audio on a blocking task)

commands.returns: MelSpec { width, height, data: number[] (f32, width*height), beatGrid: BeatGrid | null }
sideEffects: decodes the whole track (or reads the decode cache keyed by trackHash) on a spawn_blocking worker
commands.notes: DEAD from the frontend: registered at src-tauri/src/lib.rs:476, no TS caller — mel specs reach the UI through run_graph's `melSpecs` map instead. Always returns `beatGrid: null` from this path even though the struct carries the field (run_graph's mel specs are the ones that populate it) — a dead field on this route. Dimensions are fixed constants (MEL_SPEC_WIDTH/HEIGHT), not parameters. Payload is a flat f32 array, not base64.

commands.name: composite_track

rust.service: compositor::build_scene → eval::compile::compile_pattern + eval::context::build_resident_context; installs on RenderEngine

args.name: annotations
args.type: LiveAnnotation[] | null — { id, patternId, startTime: f64, endTime: f64, zIndex: i64, blendMode: BlendMode, args: JSON (default {}) }

args.name: skipCache
args.type: boolean | undefined (DEAD — bound to `_skip_cache`, never read)

sideEffects: render_engine.set_active_scene(Some(scene)) — replaces the live render scene; set_active_scene(None) when annotations are empty or the built scene is empty
clear_plan_cache() when the annotation list is empty
reads/writes the process-global PLAN_CACHE (per-annotation compiled plan keyed by id + signature over pattern_id, venue_id, implementation_id, graph_revision, start/end, args) — incremental recompile
checks COMPOSITING_GENERATION before and after building; a concurrent leave_track/cancel_compositing makes the pass a no-op
resolves fixtures root + StorageRoot from AppHandle
commands.notes: annotations semantics are load-bearing: `null`/omitted ⇒ fall back to persisted scores (sorted z_index asc); `[]` ⇒ authoritative empty document, clears the scene (this is how deleting the last clip clears output). Callers always send the full live list (mid-drag args ahead of the DB). z_index and blend_mode are Scene metadata and deliberately excluded from the plan signature. The rAF-coalesced live path (store:499) fires per frame, so the command must be cheap and idempotent.

commands.name: leave_track
sideEffects: bumps COMPOSITING_GENERATION (aborts any in-flight composite_track)
clear_plan_cache()
render_engine.set_active_scene(None)
host.unload() — unloads decoded audio
stem_cache.remove_track(track_id)
commands.notes: Takes the SCORE id, not the track id — the track id is resolved host-side via `SELECT track_id FROM scores WHERE id = ?` under VenueAccess::<Read> on VenueResource::Score. Fails if the score row is gone, so a port must call it before deleting the score. Both call sites fire-and-forget (`.catch(console.error)`) and only invoke when trackId and scoreId are both non-null.

commands.name: generate_annotation_previews
commands.returns: AnnotationPreview[] — { annotationId, width, height, pixels: u8[] (RGBA), dominantColor: [f32,f32,f32] }
sideEffects: read-only w.r.t. the DB; compiles + evaluates every annotation's pattern (CPU heavy)
resolves fixtures root + StorageRoot from AppHandle; may read audio/stem assets via build_resident_context
commands.notes: One entry per persisted score row, in fetch order (z_index asc). Empty-graph annotations still yield an entry via empty_preview(). Returns [] when the track has no annotations. `pixels` crosses IPC as a JSON number array (Vec<u8>, no base64/serde_bytes) — the store feeds it straight to `new Uint8ClampedArray(...)` + ImageData + createImageBitmap. Width = STEPS_PER_BEAT(16) columns/beat clamped to [8,512]; height ≤ 32 rows (rows = fixtures, cols = time). Store closes previous ImageBitmaps before replacing (GPU leak otherwise) and bumps a generation counter.

commands.name: preview_annotation

args.name: annotation
args.type: LivePreviewInput — { id, patternId, startTime: f32, endTime: f32, args: JSON (default {}) }

sideEffects: read-only; compile + eval of one pattern over the preview column grid
commands.notes: Single-annotation version of generate_annotation_previews, driven live during a drag. LivePreviewInput has NO zIndex/blendMode (unlike compositor::LiveAnnotation) — the preview is always rendered alone with blend Replace, z 0, so it is per-clip output, not composite output. Host fills unset args from the pattern's arg defaults; the caller only sends overrides. Returned annotationId echoes the input id. Store coalesces: one in-flight call per annotation id, latest pending call replayed on completion.

commands.name: get_venue_annotation_counts

rust.service: inline sqlx query over scores JOIN track_scores (no service layer)

sideEffects: VenueAccess::<Read> on the venue
commands.notes: Sparse map: tracks with zero annotations in this venue are ABSENT, so callers must default to 0 (the store does `counts[t.id] ?? 0`). Overlaps list_tracks_enriched's venueAnnotationCount — the same number by two code paths, one of them raw SQL embedded in the command file instead of database/local/tracks.rs. That is the smell: it exists purely as a cheap refresh of one column after a venue switch.

commands.name: get_track_waveform
commands.returns: TrackWaveform { trackId, uid: string|null, previewSamples: number[], fullSamples: number[]|null, bands: BandEnvelopes|null, previewBands: BandEnvelopes|null, colors: number[]|null, previewColors: number[]|null, sampleRate: number, durationSeconds: number }
sideEffects: Takes an AnalysisTaskGroup lease/epoch guard (cancellable analysis work)
On cache miss: decodes the audio file and computes the waveform, then upserts blobs into the local waveforms table and commits (ensure_track_waveform)
Logs '[waveform] track {id} published in {ms}ms' to stderr
Fails if the authenticated principal changes or track_hash changes mid-computation
commands.notes: Read-through cache, not a pure read: first call for a track can take seconds and writes to the DB. Samples are interleaved min/max pairs per bucket (previewSamples.length = 2*buckets); bands/colors are the two generations of the same idea (colors is legacy interleaved RGB bytes). fullSamples/bands/colors are NOT cloud-synced — regenerated locally, so they can be null on a freshly pulled device. durationSeconds prefers decoded_duration and falls back to the tracks.duration_seconds metadata; callers (use-track-editor-store) use it as the timeline duration. All TS callers .catch(() => null) — treat failure as 'no waveform', not fatal.

commands.name: get_track_waveform_window
commands.returns: WaveformWindow { trackId, startSeconds, endSeconds, min: number[], max: number[], rms: number[] } — the three series are the same length, and it is the requested bucket count clamped to 1..=16384
sideEffects: VisibleTrackAccess::<Read> on the track, to read file_path/track_hash

Decodes the audio through audio::cache (process-wide LRU over the on-disk .pcm cache) on a blocking thread if it is not already resident — the same (hash, device rate) key host_load_track uses, so a track loaded for playback is already there
Writes nothing
commands.notes: The fine half of the waveform pair: get_track_waveform is a fixed 30 000 buckets however long the track is, this is exactly the visible range at exactly the caller's pixel density, measured from the audio each time. No AnalysisTaskGroup lease and no DB write — it is a view of the audio, not a stored artifact. Total by construction: the range is clamped to the decoded audio (the returned startSeconds/endSeconds are the clamped range, not the requested one) and the bucket count to 1..=16384, so a request past either end is answered rather than refused. Only the GPUI editor calls it today; the web timeline can adopt it unchanged, and should above ~FULL_WAVEFORM_SIZE/duration pixels per second, which is where its stored envelope runs out of buckets.

commands.name: reprocess_waveform
sideEffects: Unconditionally recomputes from audio (skips the cache check) and upserts the waveform blobs
Same AnalysisTaskGroup lease + principal/hash guards as get_track_waveform
commands.notes: Identical to get_track_waveform minus the cache lookup — both funnel into ensure_track_waveform. Caller pushes the result straight into useTrackEditorStore ({ waveform, durationSeconds }) only if the track is still the active one; a port must keep that staleness check or the editor shows another track's waveform.

commands.name: render_identify

rust.service: RenderEngine::identify_targets, authorized by local authorize_identify_targets → VenueAccess<Read> on VenueResource::Fixture(first target)

sideEffects: installs an IdentifyState { targets, start: Instant::now() } that drives a two-blink sequence in both the visualizer and ArtNet output
commands.notes: The only command in this fragment with NO venueId argument — the venue is derived from the fixture ids and every target must resolve to the same venue, otherwise it fails as one opaque not-found. Target grammar is `"fixtureId"` (whole fixture) or `"fixtureId:headIndex"`. Empty targets vector is an error at the authorize layer ("Identify requires at least one fixture target") but a no-op inside identify_targets — two contradictory guards. Callers fire-and-forget.

commands.name: get_fixture_definition
commands.returns: FixtureDefinition — PascalCase-ish serde shape: { Manufacturer, Model, Type, Channel: Channel[], Mode: Mode[], Physical }
sideEffects: Reads and parses a QLC+-style fixture XML file from disk each call (no server-side cache)
commands.notes: `path` is relative to the fixtures root and is joined without sanitization — a port should reject absolute/`..` paths. The serde/TS shape is the raw XML mapping (keys like "@Name", "$value") and is the ONE place that convention leaks into TS; everything else is camelCase. Frontend caches definitions in a Map keyed by path (definitionsCache) — two call sites, one for the cache and one for the selected-entry preview, both use the same command.

commands.name: get_patch_hierarchy
commands.returns: Vec<FixtureNode> — { id, label, type: "fixture"|"head", children: FixtureNode[] }
sideEffects: VenueAccess::<Read>; parses each fixture's definition XML from disk to enumerate heads
commands.notes: DEAD on the TS side — registered in lib.rs:511 but no caller anywhere in src/ or scripts/. Head node ids are `${fixtureId}:${headIndex}` (the same composite convention groups use). Definition parse failures are silently swallowed (fixture appears with no children). Label falls back to `${manufacturer} ${model}` when label is null. Overlaps heavily with get_grouped_hierarchy — a port should decide whether it survives.

commands.name: get_patched_fixtures
sideEffects: VenueAccess::<Read> on the venue
Not a pure read: also pushes the loaded patch into ArtNetManager (clone of the fixture list) when that state exists
commands.notes: The workhorse refetch — every mutating fixture command in the store is followed by fetchPatchedFixtures(), which also prunes selection state to ids that still exist. Agent ask-venue-tool pairs it with get_grouped_hierarchy to build the venue dump. Because it side-effects the ArtNet patch, a port must not treat it as a cacheable GET.

commands.name: initialize_fixtures
commands.returns: usize — number of fixture definitions indexed
sideEffects: Walks the resolved fixtures root on disk (resolve_fixtures_root: bundled resource dir, else dev path) and builds a FixtureIndex
Replaces the in-memory FixtureState (Mutex<Option<FixtureIndex>>) managed state
commands.notes: No args at all — state comes from the AppHandle. Must run before search_fixtures (which errors 'Fixtures not initialized. Call initialize_fixtures first.'). Store ignores the returned count and immediately fires search('', true) then fetchPatchedFixtures(). Errors are swallowed by the caller.

commands.name: move_patched_fixture
sideEffects: VenueAccess::<Write> on VenueResource::Fixture(id) + access.require_venue(venue_id)
require_changed: errors 'Venue resource not found' unless exactly 1 row updated
Re-pushes the whole patch to ArtNet; invalidate_venue_fixture_cache()
commands.notes: DMX address move only, despite the generic name (spatial move is the separate _spatial command). venue_id is a redundant authorization cross-check — the write scope is the fixture. Caller optimistically sets `address: BigInt(address)` then refetches on both success and failure.

commands.name: move_patched_fixture_spatial
sideEffects: VenueAccess::<Write> on the fixture + require_venue; require_changed (1 row or error)
Re-reads the patch and pushes it to ArtNet on every call; invalidate_venue_fixture_cache()
commands.notes: Absolute pose, not a delta — multi-select drag/rotate computes each fixture's new absolute pos/rot in TS and fires one invoke per fixture via Promise.all (no batch command). Each of those calls re-reads the full patch and re-pushes ArtNet: O(n) full-patch reads for an n-fixture drag. Rotation is Euler XYZ radians in the app's Z-up-ish convention (same fields as StagePiece). Callers update state optimistically and refetch on error.

commands.name: patch_fixture

rust.service: database::local::fixtures::insert_fixture (inline in the command, not a service fn)

commands.returns: PatchedFixture { id, uid: string|null, venueId, universe: bigint, address: bigint, numChannels: bigint, manufacturer, model, modeName, fixturePath, label: string|null, posX..posZ, rotX..rotZ }
sideEffects: VenueAccess::<Write> on VenueResource::Venue(venue_id); inserts a row and commits
Re-reads the full patch and pushes it to ArtNetManager (fixture_service::update_artnet_patch) — live DMX output changes
invalidate_venue_fixture_cache()
commands.notes: No address-overlap validation server-side — the frontend computes the next free address (findNextAvailableAddress) and the auto label `${model} (${n+1})`. Spatial pose is NOT settable here: duplicate flows patch first, then call move_patched_fixture_spatial to copy the pose. universe/address/numChannels are i64 on the wire but bigint in the TS type, so callers must pass plain numbers in and Number()-convert on the way back out (see :688 `universe: Number(fixture.universe)`). One call site ignores the return and refetches; two use the returned fixture's id.

commands.name: remove_patched_fixture
sideEffects: VenueAccess::<Write> on the fixture + require_venue; require_changed (1 row or error)
Deletes the fixture row (group membership rows presumably cascade); re-pushes patch to ArtNet; invalidate_venue_fixture_cache()
commands.notes: Single-fixture only; bulk delete is a Promise.all fan-out in the store (:623). Caller drops the id from selectedPatchedIds/lastSelectedPatchedId before refetching.

commands.name: rename_patched_fixture
sideEffects: VenueAccess::<Write> on the fixture + require_venue; require_changed
Re-pushes patch to ArtNet; invalidate_venue_fixture_cache()
commands.notes: label is non-optional String here even though the column is nullable — there's no way to clear a label back to null via this command. Frontend trims and refuses empty. After success the caller refetches fixtures AND useGroupStore.fetchGroups(venueId), because labels are denormalized into the group hierarchy.

commands.name: search_fixtures
commands.returns: Vec<FixtureEntry> — { manufacturer: string, model: string, path: string }[]
sideEffects: None (pure read of the in-memory index; locks the FixtureState mutex)
commands.notes: Synchronous (non-async) command. Empty query = plain paging over the whole index; otherwise a lowercase substring match on manufacturer OR model — no fuzzy ranking, index order is preserved. Note skip(offset) is applied AFTER filtering, so offset is an offset into the filtered result set. Store pages with LIMIT=50-style constant, tracks pageOffset += results.length and infers hasMore = results.length === LIMIT. `path` is the key for get_fixture_definition and the fixturePath stored on a patched fixture.

commands.name: add_fixture_to_group
sideEffects: VenueAccess::<Write> on VenueResource::Group(group_id) ONLY — the fixture is not separately authorized
Inserts a membership row; invalidate_venue_fixture_cache()
commands.notes: head_index = None means whole-fixture membership and is stored as the sentinel groups_db::WHOLE_FIXTURE, not NULL — a port must keep that sentinel, since remove_fixture_from_group's split logic depends on it. Adding a head to a fixture that already has whole-fixture membership is subsumed server-side, so the store only does an optimistic update for whole-fixture adds and refetches the hierarchy for head adds (and refetches on error too).

commands.name: create_group

rust.service: database::local::groups::create_group (uniqueness check inline in the command)

commands.returns: FixtureGroup { id, uid, venueId, name: string|null, axisLr/axisFb/axisAb: number|null, movementConfig: MovementConfig|null, displayOrder: bigint, createdAt, updatedAt }
sideEffects: VenueAccess::<Write> on the venue
Pre-check: lists all groups and rejects with "A group with name 'x' already exists" if normalize_group_name collides (in-transaction, not a DB unique constraint)
invalidate_venue_fixture_cache()
commands.notes: Names are normalized (lowercase, spaces/hyphens -> underscore, non-alnum stripped, collapsed) for uniqueness but the raw name is stored; the error message quotes the *normalized* form. Empty-normalized names skip the check entirely, so multiple such groups are allowed. Axes are LR/FB/AB in -1..+1. movementConfig can't be set at create — it goes through update_movement_config. Caller optimistically appends a synthetic FixtureGroupNode with fixtureType 'unknown' and empty fixtures.

commands.name: delete_group
sideEffects: VenueAccess::<Write> on the group; require_changed -> 'Venue resource not found' if not exactly 1 row
Membership rows go away with the group (FK cascade); invalidate_venue_fixture_cache()
commands.notes: Caller optimistically removes the group and clears selectedGroupId, reverting to the captured previousGroups on error; returns boolean success to the UI. Deleting a group referenced by a saved selection expression is not checked — dangling name references stay dangling.

commands.name: get_group
sideEffects: VenueAccess::<Read> on VenueResource::Group(id)
commands.notes: DEAD on the TS side — registered at lib.rs:524 but nothing in src/ or scripts/ invokes it. Every frontend path reads groups via list_groups or get_grouped_hierarchy.

commands.name: get_grouped_hierarchy
commands.returns: FixtureGroupNode[] — { groupId, groupName: string|null, fixtureType, axisLr|axisFb|axisAb: number|null, movementConfig: MovementConfig|null, fixtures: GroupedFixtureNode[] } where GroupedFixtureNode = { id, label, fixtureType, heads: HeadNode[], headCount }
sideEffects: read-only; VenueAccess::<Read> on VenueResource::Venue(venueId)
commands.notes: camelCase JSON (serde rename_all). Service needs the AppHandle to reach the bundled fixture-definition resource root, so a port must supply a resource path, not just a pool. groupName is nullable — pattern-editor filters nulls before building its group-name list. `heads.length < headCount` means partial-fixture membership.

commands.name: get_ungrouped_fixtures
sideEffects: read-only; VenueAccess::<Read> on the venue
commands.notes: Fixtures in the venue with no group membership row at all (whole-fixture or per-head). Filed under 'Migration / Maintenance' in the Rust file — it exists to surface fixtures left behind by the group migration.

commands.name: list_groups
sideEffects: VenueAccess::<Read> on the venue
commands.notes: The flat sibling of get_grouped_hierarchy (which the group store uses). Two of the three callers only want `name` and filter out nulls (group names are nullable, so the selection-expression vocabulary is a filtered subset); group-expression-editor also dedupes and sorts. Ordering comes from the DB (displayOrder) and is relied on implicitly by perform-page's flat group list.

commands.name: preview_selection_query
commands.returns: PatchedFixture[] (the resolver's ResolvedFixture list mapped to .fixture, order = resolver order)
sideEffects: read-only; VenueAccess::<Read> on the venue
commands.notes: seed defaults to 12345 when absent — deterministic randomness for `random()` selectors, so a port MUST keep the same default or previews drift from evaluation. query is `.trim()`ed host-side. Store swallows errors and returns [] — invalid selection syntax is indistinguishable from an empty match at the call site (smell).

commands.name: remove_fixture_from_group

rust.service: database::local::groups::remove_member_from_group (whole fixture) | services::groups::remove_head_from_group (single head, needs fixtures resource root)

sideEffects: VenueAccess::<Write> on VenueResource::Group(groupId) — authorization + tx; access.commit()
invalidate_venue_fixture_cache() (process-global fixture cache)
headIndex=null drops the whole membership incl. per-head rows; headIndex=N on a whole-fixture membership SPLITS it into per-head rows for the remaining heads (writes N-1 rows)
resolves fixtures resource root from AppHandle in the per-head branch only
commands.notes: TS sends headIndex as `headIndex ?? null` — null is meaningful (whole fixture), not 'omitted'. The store does an optimistic local removal, and refetches the whole hierarchy after a per-head removal (because the split changes structure) and on any error. Group-scoped auth: the group id, not the venue id, is the resource.

commands.name: update_group
sideEffects: VenueAccess::<Write> on the group
Same normalized-name collision pre-check as create_group, excluding self
invalidate_venue_fixture_cache()
commands.notes: Ambiguous None semantics: it is unclear from the command whether None means 'leave unchanged' or 'set null' — the caller always sends all four fields explicitly (`?? null`), so the frontend behaves as if it's a full replace. Its optimistic update disagrees with that: it applies `axisLr ?? g.axisLr` locally (keep-old) while sending null. Ordering/movementConfig are not updatable here. No venue_id arg — scope comes from the group.

commands.name: update_movement_config

args.name: config
args.type: MovementConfig | null — { baseDirX, baseDirY, baseDirZ, extentU, extentV, uvRotation } all f64

sideEffects: VenueAccess::<Write> on VenueResource::Group(groupId); commit
invalidate_venue_fixture_cache()
commands.notes: config: null CLEARS the movement config (sets the column NULL) — it is not 'leave unchanged'. Defaults if a port needs them: baseDir (0,0,-1) straight down, extentU/V 30°, uvRotation 0; Z-up coordinate system, extents are half-widths in degrees. Store updates optimistically and refetches the hierarchy on error; the returned FixtureGroup is discarded by the caller.

commands.name: create_venue
commands.returns: Venue { id, uid, name, description, shareCode, role, controllerPort, mixerPort, mixerMappingJson, createdAt, updatedAt } (serde camelCase)
sideEffects: inserts a local venue row (role='owner'), marked dirty for the sync pusher
commands.notes: Unlike update/delete, this one does NOT go through VenueAccess — it takes the pool directly (no venue exists yet to lock). description is nullable: the TS store coerces empty string to null (`description || null`). Caller ignores the returned Venue's freshness and immediately re-invokes list_venues via refresh().

commands.name: delete_venue
sideEffects: BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction + commit
local venue row removed / tombstoned; sync push propagates
commands.notes: Owner-side delete. No cloud call here (contrast leave_venue, which does hit Supabase directly). Caller clears selectedVenueId when the deleted id was selected — note the caller compares `String(get().selectedVenueId) === id`, a stringify guard that hints selectedVenueId was once numeric.

commands.name: get_or_create_share_code
sideEffects: requires an authenticated session (errors 'Not authenticated')
owner-only: errors if venue.uid != current user id
generates + persists share_code locally (VenueAccess::<Write>, committed)
PATCHes venues.share_code to Supabase with the user's access token; a cloud failure is only eprintln'd, not returned
commands.notes: Idempotent: returns the existing code if one is already set (no cloud write in that path). The cloud write is best-effort — a local code can exist that the cloud never learned about, so join_venue would fail for it; that is a real drift hazard for a port. Caller auto-invokes on first dialog open and only console.errors on failure.

commands.name: get_venue
commands.returns: Venue — { id, uid: string|null, name, description: string|null, shareCode: string|null, role: "owner"|"member", controllerPort: string|null, mixerPort: string|null, mixerMappingJson: string|null, createdAt, updatedAt } (camelCase)
sideEffects: read-only; VenueAccess::<Read> on VenueResource::Venue(id) — errors if the venue is not accessible to the current principal
commands.notes: Argument is `id`, not `venueId` (inconsistent with every other command in this fragment, which uses venueId). All three route wrappers re-fetch on every mount rather than reusing store state — deliberate, because `role` can change between sessions. The three call sites are literally the same effect copy-pasted three times (dedupe candidate).

commands.name: join_venue
sideEffects: requires auth
remote RPC join_venue_by_code creates the cloud membership row
inserts a local venue row whose id IS the cloud UUID and whose uid is the OWNER's uid, not the joiner's
commands.notes: The uid-is-owner convention is load-bearing: is_owner() is decided by `role`, not by uid. Fixtures/groups/tracks are NOT pulled here — the frontend must fire sync_full after joining (join-venue-dialog.tsx:48 does exactly that, fire-and-forget). Errors from the RPC are wrapped as 'Failed to join venue: …'.

commands.name: leave_venue
sideEffects: read access opened then explicitly dropped before the network call (holds no transaction across IO)
errors 'Cannot leave a venue you own' when venue.is_owner()
requires auth; DELETEs venue_members where venue_id=eq.X&user_id=eq.Y in Supabase (failure only eprintln'd)
removes the local membership row
commands.notes: Ordering matters: ownership check → drop read txn → cloud delete → local delete. The cloud delete is best-effort, so a port must tolerate a local-left/cloud-still-member state (next pull could re-add). Venue row itself survives if other memberships remain.

commands.name: list_venues
sideEffects: read-only
commands.notes: No VenueAccess wrapper — scoping lives in the SQL instead: it CROSS JOINs auth_write_admission and returns rows only while admission is armed/accepting/not-maintenance, matching venue.uid against admission.active_uid (guest ⇒ uid IS NULL AND role != 'member'). Consequence a port must keep: while write admission is closed (mid identity switch / sign-out) this returns an EMPTY list, not an error. `role` is COMPUTED per query from active_uid, not read from the stored column. Takes no arguments; the headless scripts still pass `{}`. Result order is unspecified — nothing re-sorts.

commands.name: update_venue
sideEffects: BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction on the local sqlite pool, committed explicitly via access.commit()
bumps updated_at → row becomes dirty → picked up by the sync pusher
commands.notes: name is required (full replace, not a patch — there is no partial-update path; passing an empty name would blank it). description null-coerced by the caller. Write access enforces venue permissions before the update; failure surfaces as a plain error String.

issues.summary: Registered commands with zero TS callers. Categories can be listed and assigned from the UI but never created; mel specs only reach the UI via run_graph's melSpecs map. See deadCommands for the full registry-level list.

One concept, two event names and two payload shapes: import_track's pipeline emits `track-import-progress` as a positional tuple (trackId, step); import_tracks emits `file-import-progress` as a structured ImportProgressEvent. Unify on the structured shape.
Parameter naming drift: set_pattern_category takes `patternId` while every other pattern command takes `id`.

set_pattern_category is the only pattern mutation that does not call engine.push_notify.notify_one(), so a category change is not pushed until an unrelated write wakes the sync loop. Both it and verify_pattern return void, forcing a get_pattern read-after-write.

update_pattern is a full replace, not a patch. Callers fill untouched fields from possibly-stale local state (`name: pattern?.name ?? ""`), so renaming with an unloaded pattern can blank the name. It also bypasses AuthoredDocuments and writes the SQLite projection directly, unlike create/delete.

get_pattern_args loads the whole graph document and discards everything but `.args` — same cost as get_pattern_graph_document. Worse, get_pattern_graph_document passes venue_id = None while get_pattern_args passes a real venue, so the two can resolve DIFFERENT implementations for the same pattern id.
get_venue_annotation_counts duplicates list_tracks_enriched's venueAnnotationCount as raw SQL embedded in the command file instead of living in database/local/tracks.rs.
The has* flags fall back to artifact version 0 when the registry has no preprocessor for a table, and version 0 matches any row — so hasX can read true for a stale artifact.
get_melspec always returns beatGrid: null on that route; the field is only populated by run_graph's mel specs. Dead field on the command.
Unused injected State params: run_graph takes `_stem_cache`; preview_pattern takes both `_stem_cache` and `_fft_service`.

Silently clamps fps into [10,30] and frame_count into [1,256], so long spans under-sample with no signal to the caller. It also forces every Selection arg to "all", so preview output can differ materially from a real run.

The TS wrapper (src/lib/dsl/index.ts:51) blind-retries the identical request exactly once on ANY failure. That is only safe because operationId makes the write idempotent — an invariant undocumented at the call site that any port must preserve.
Takes VenueAccess::<Write> for the scope check then drops it before the authored apply — a TOCTOU window between authorization and write.

The caller (pattern-editor.tsx:1755) passes an opaque `input` object straight into invoke, so the TS object keys ARE the Rust arg names with no typecheck between them. Renaming a Rust arg breaks the call silently at runtime.

Fragment authors split src-tauri/src/commands/groups.rs across two domain labels (`stage/groups` and `universe/groups`). Canonicalized here to universe/groups; the underlying file is one module and should stay one domain.

`controller_port_change` (controller_manager.rs:295) is emitted and never listened to. `universe-buffer` and `dmx://update` are the mirror image — the visualizer stores subscribe to them but nothing in src-tauri/ has ever emitted them; delete the listeners. (`close-requested` is not in this set: Tauri's own window lifecycle emits it.)
